# Artifacts and storage

Use the relevant sections when starting a project, assigning file ownership and locations, running checks or experiments, preparing deliverables, or deciding retention and cleanup. Apply [task and decision authority](../SKILL.md#fit-the-actual-task) throughout. Save important storage discussion under [automatic documentation](records-and-handoff.md#maintain-documents-throughout-the-work), using pending content when writes are restricted. Reorganization of existing stores, deletion, publication and changes to product retention requirements need their applicable authorization.

| Need | Section |
| --- | --- |
| Start a project or introduce a new data type | [Storage policy](#plan-storage-when-the-project-starts) and [classification](#classify-by-responsibility). |
| Place project files or adapt a layout to its framework | [Ownership and selection order](#choose-ownership-before-creating-files). |
| Reorganize existing project folders or files | [Project-file organization](#organize-existing-project-files), then affected ownership and directory rules. |
| Choose output paths and run checks | [Layout](#use-a-concrete-layout) and [batch protocol](#manage-each-batch-from-creation-to-closeout). |
| A temporary helper becomes a dependency, or directories need creation/retirement | [Maintained ownership](#establish-maintained-ownership-when-dependencies-appear) and [directory lifecycle](#create-and-retire-directories-deliberately), as applicable. |
| Preserve results or reduce generated files | [Evidence and cleanup](#select-evidence-and-clean-up-within-authority) and affected [repository self-containment](#make-repository-records-self-contained). |
| Make records usable from GitHub or another repository host | [Repository self-containment](#make-repository-records-self-contained). |
| Relate a review package or output to source | [Version and artifact identity](#distinguish-source-versions-from-execution-evidence); [review packages](review-packages.md) owns archive delivery mechanics. |

## Plan storage when the project starts

Before the first work that creates relevant data or artifacts, establish their destinations and lifecycle within the authorized setup or development batch. A new project has no inherited storage contract: select the necessary arrangement rather than referring to a policy that does not exist. Plan the categories about to be used, without designing a complete storage platform or creating empty directories for future features.

Use `docs/ARTIFACT_STORAGE.md` as the default policy owner. Reuse an explicitly mapped existing owner, or a clearly identified README section for a small self-contained tool, when it supplies the same information. Register the owner in the central document entry and route applicable agent/setup guidance to it. Keep storage decisions with their reasons there, or link to the existing decision owner for material choices. Product persistence and recovery behavior stays in its contract/design owner; the storage policy links to that behavior.

For each applicable category, a short table and necessary explanations must identify:

- Purpose, producer/consumer, actual path or path pattern, and applicable creation conditions or tool constraints, including tool-native or external storage when applicable.
- The authoritative retained copy, and which other locations are copies, packages or derivatives.
- Version-control and access/sharing policy, including private inputs and local settings. Keep credentials out of committed records and manifests.
- Source/input identity and how to recover or regenerate content; state what cannot be reconstructed.
- Retention, backup/recovery responsibilities where needed, ownership-transition and retirement/cleanup conditions, and applicable authority; identify active use, unique evidence and user modifications as exceptions to disposable defaults.

Set the policy once and apply it in subsequent work. Update it when a new category, material storage arrangement or preservation responsibility appears, not for every command. Class-level rules cover ordinary files; record only meaningful item-specific exceptions. Apply settled choices without new approval rounds. Unresolved choices that materially change preservation, recovery, sharing or other agreed boundaries follow the skill's human-decision rule; routine path selection within them is autonomous.

## Classify by responsibility

| Category | Typical content and location examples | Responsibility to establish |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Maintained project assets | Source in its application/package module; tests and shareable fixtures in their test owner; specifications/decisions in `docs/`; reusable commands in `tools/` or `scripts/`; maintained research in its declared owner | Create or generate adopted assets directly in their owner when work starts, distinguishing editable sources from generated outputs. Preserve version identity and reviewable changes. |
| External inputs and local settings | Original datasets, references and private configuration in declared input/configuration locations, such as `data/raw/`, `references/` or protected storage | Original location/provenance, access, sharing and preservation requirements, established when importing or creating them. |
| Persistent task data | Databases, task state and user edits in the selected store, such as `workspaces/` or an app's platform data location | Durable storage, recovery, backup and deletion responsibility, established before task creation. |
| Verification records and evidence | Maintained results in `docs/verification/` or its mapped owner; logs, failed cases, screenshots and source snapshots in declared evidence/batch locations | Exact execution association, supported conclusions and retained evidence. Follow the document authority and timing rules. |
| Build and delivery artifacts | Builds, installers, exports and review packages in configured locations such as `build/`, `dist/`, `out/`, `release/` or `outputs/` | Establish source/build identity and delivery destination before building/exporting; retain publication state. |
| Regenerable caches and environments | Dependency caches, tool downloads, build caches and disposable environments in their supported locations | Create when an actual workflow needs them; record reuse, regeneration inputs and invalidation/cleanup conditions. |
| Temporary working data | Test workspaces, extraction staging and intermediate files in an isolated batch or tool temporary location | Allocate for the bounded operation; select necessary results before disposition. |

These are responsibilities, not seven mandatory directories. Use suitable framework, operating-system and tool conventions, including native output/cache locations. Explain a material departure; a confusing inherited layout can be improved within reorganization authority. A file with multiple roles has one authoritative retained location with references from other roles. Explicitly required backups are separate from accidental duplication. A directory name, age, ignored status or failed run alone does not establish disposability or permanent value.

## Choose ownership before creating files

Determine the intended consumer (application, tests/CI, build, maintainer, user or a bounded investigation), whether the content is adopted for continuing use, whether it contains unique observations/originals/user edits, and any tool constraints on location, naming or cleanup. Apply established class-level rules; this is not a per-file form.

Within effective requirements and authority, choose a location in this order:

1. Check the selected tool/framework version's required discovery, lifecycle, packaging and native-storage behavior. Distinguish required behavior from optional recommendations. Reuse applicable research; follow [design research guidance](implementation.md#choose-a-durable-design) for initial/material choices and uncertain behavior, without surveying every ecosystem for routine files.
2. Apply the project's adopted ownership map when it satisfies those constraints. Prefer a fitting existing module or package owner, including colocated tests or feature files where appropriate. A confusing or incompatible arrangement can be revised within scope; identify conflicts rather than silently following either a broken map or a generic example.
3. Where no arrangement is selected, use applicable supported conventions, then the responsibility-based examples above for remaining gaps. Record actual paths and consequential reasons in the policy. Resolve ordinary organization details autonomously; material behavior, recovery, preservation or scope tradeoffs require the applicable human choice unless delegated.

When work is already adopted as a maintained feature, regression test, operational tool or project document, create or generate it directly in the appropriate owner. Do not stage all development in `.local` and rely on a later cleanup to discover formal assets. Exploratory work is not automatically disposable: a research notebook can be a maintained deliverable, and an original observation can be required evidence. Generated content can also be a lasting result. Use intended responsibility, dependencies and preservation requirements, not exploratory/generated labels alone.

For code, documents or other artifacts intended to be maintained by regeneration, distinguish the editable source of truth (such as a schema, template or configuration) from its outputs. Identify the inputs, generator and relevant version, regeneration command, output locations and supported customization/extension points in the existing owner or build instructions. Change the maintained inputs and regenerate within authority; a generated file's location or tracked status does not make it the correct editing target. If direct output edits are part of a selected workflow, state how they survive regeneration or why regeneration no longer applies. Decide whether to version outputs from the build and delivery requirements, without making all generated content disposable or requiring it all in Git.

Storage location, Git inclusion, build/package inclusion and external transmission are separate decisions: private input or persistent task data may have a formal location while remaining ignored. When introducing or changing a build, packaging, deployment/upload flow or a storage arrangement that affects it, check the tool's actual input and inclusion rules and applicable filters or allowlists. `.gitignore` and directory names such as `.local` are not general exclusion guarantees: Docker build contexts use `.dockerignore`, while npm has `files`/`.npmignore` rules and only conditionally uses `.gitignore`. Establish which files the affected flow includes or transmits and verify the intended selection within authority; reuse applicable verified rules for routine work. Inspection and package preparation themselves follow the [command-effect boundary](review.md#scope-and-authority) and do not authorize publication.

Ordinary checkout/build/test operation should not depend on an undeclared local-batch helper; declared private inputs still need an access/setup route and honest availability limits. A write scope restricted to scratch or local analysis does not authorize editing a formal owner; record the intended destination and any unresolved dependency instead.

## Use a concrete layout

When a project has no suitable arrangement, use this default for development batches, creating only the needed files and directories:

```text
docs/ARTIFACT_STORAGE.md
docs/verification/YYYYMMDD_HHMM_<TOPIC>.md
.local/runs/YYYYMMDD_HHMM_<TOPIC>/
  README.md
  reports/
  evidence/
  scratch/
```

`reports/` holds execution logs and machine reports; `evidence/` holds selected retained cases, outputs or necessary source snapshots; `scratch/` holds temporary work. Put batch-only helpers in that batch, using `scripts/` when useful. An artifact's directory does not override its declared preservation requirements. Keep distinct executions identifiable, for example `reports/check-01.log` and `scratch/check-01/`, rather than guessing later from `final`, `final2` or modification times. Follow the existing [timestamp, timezone and collision rules](documentation-structure.md#name-active-and-dated-records) for batch identities; do not rename historical evidence merely to match this example.

The policy also maps any persistent task stores, private inputs, exports, builds and caches that the project actually needs. Paths such as `.local/tasks/`, `.local/exports/` and `.local/cache/` are options; a desktop app may need its platform data directory and a build tool its native output path. Do not force all storage into `.local` or relocate managed environments simply for visual uniformity.

Keep a concise whole-project responsibility map in README or the declared project entry, linking to the storage policy and existing document catalogue. The map includes maintained assets, task/input stores, generated outputs and external/native locations where applicable; it is not a second complete file inventory. Paths in this reference illustrate a mapping, not a universal directory tree.

The batch entry identifies its purpose, executions and artifact locations and links to its maintained verification record. Existing tool reports or an adequate manifest may supply execution details; do not duplicate them into a new mandatory schema. An adequate existing task/verification record can serve as the entry; a routine check needs no new Markdown file or batch directory when established locations and execution association suffice. A local index such as `.local/INDEX.md` can list physical batches, purpose, status, entry links and retention reasons. It is subordinate to the central document catalogue, contains no sole copy of essential policy or conclusions, and need not enumerate every raw file. Link large collections through a suitable manifest.

## Establish maintained ownership when dependencies appear

Reassess a batch-only helper, case or result as soon as any of these applies:

- Maintained application code, tests, CI or build workflows begin to import, invoke or otherwise rely on it.
- Maintained guidance names it as a normal operating or development step.
- It is adopted as a continuing tool, regression case, maintained research asset or deliverable.
- A new maintainer needs it for the documented normal development/operation workflow.

Within the authorized batch, establish its appropriate owner before handing off that dependency: make the content suitable for the selected purpose, verify it proportionately, update callers/instructions and preserve the link to its originating evidence. Handle superseded copies under the retention policy. Where scope or authority prevents completion, report the intended owner and the unresolved dependency rather than claiming a self-contained workflow. Do not wait for an arbitrary reuse count or build a general tool because something might become useful. Citing an earlier run does not turn all its raw products into maintained code or fixtures; preserve those under their evidence/data roles.

## Create and retire directories deliberately

Create a directory when its first actual content needs that responsibility, or a selected tool/deployment/storage contract requires it to exist in advance. Before adding it, check for a suitable existing owner; avoid competing `tools/`, `scripts/` and `helpers/` with overlapping, undefined roles. Clear responsibilities justify a small directory, while file count or visual symmetry does not justify empty scaffolding.

After moving or consolidating content, inspect affected imports, discovery/build/package rules, tests/CI, configuration and documentation links, including relevant ignore/backup rules. Reconcile them and verify the affected behavior within scope. Retire an old directory only after required content and provenance are preserved and no necessary current dependency or tool requirement remains, using the applicable removal authority. An empty directory can still have a valid purpose; a user-deleted obsolete directory is not a reason to recreate it from old inventories. Preserve historical locators and disposition honestly rather than manufacturing replacement evidence.

Judge the arrangement by whether a reader can find the authoritative content and supported workflows can use it under their declared environment/access conditions. Do not optimize for filled folders, a fixed number of directories or moving every artifact into the repository.

## Organize existing project files

For `organize files`, establish the requested area, intended consumers and existing edit/move authority. Use [responsibility classification](#classify-by-responsibility), [placement selection](#choose-ownership-before-creating-files) and the adopted layout to distinguish maintained code/tests/tools/docs, inputs, persistent task data, evidence, deliverables, caches and temporary work. Do not infer disposability from a directory name, small file count or age. Empty directories are not a reason to fill out a template or move content away from its real owner.

Inspect existing changes and affected consumers before a move. A maintained helper in scratch belongs in its maintained owner when it becomes a continuing dependency; preserve any unique source and repair the path-dependent behavior. Check applicable imports, discovery, configuration, CI/build/package rules, stored paths and documentation. A cleaner tree that breaks those consumers is not a completed reorganization. Runtime/private data still follows its storage contract, and formal ownership does not mean public distribution or automatic Git inclusion.

Under authorized organization, execute routine moves and their necessary caller/navigation repairs together; verify representative affected behavior. Use [document organization](documentation-structure.md#organize-project-documents) for semantic and historical preservation when documents move. Retire directories only after the [lifecycle checks](#create-and-retire-directories-deliberately), including tool-required and active-use exceptions. Unrelated deletion follows separate [cleanup authority](#select-evidence-and-clean-up-within-authority); organization does not silently adopt a different product design or retention policy.

Report the actual owner/path changes, repaired consumers, checks, remaining dependencies and decisions. If a move crosses an unapproved data boundary or requires a material unselected method, retain the affected content and continue independent authorized organization. Do not impose a new project layout or ask permission again for ordinary details within the selected scope.

## Manage each batch from creation to closeout

An execution here is an artifact-producing check, experiment or delivery operation, not every shell/read command or individual test case. A runner's existing run/case identities may supply the association. Ordinary source/prose maintenance under established rules needs no new storage ceremony.

| Point | Required action within authority |
| --- | --- |
| Before generation | Apply the [ownership rules](#choose-ownership-before-creating-files), creating adopted project assets in their owner and allocating batch/output paths for execution products. Route batch-only helpers, test workspaces, profiles, screenshots, logs and packaging staging to their declared locations where supported. Check tool overwrite/cleanup behavior; keep durable data outside automatically cleared locations. For large suites, copies or packages, assess likely volume and duplication first. |
| Before each execution | Establish a distinct execution identity and record the actual code/input/configuration identity, relevant command/environment and intended artifact destinations. Use existing reports where adequate; never record secrets. |
| During execution and reruns | Keep outcomes associated with their execution. Preserve earlier failures and unknown costs; do not overwrite them with the latest success. Related reruns stay in the same batch unless a separate investigation or delivery purpose justifies another. |
| After results are understood | Record what happened and its limits. Select necessary evidence and representative delivery outputs; identify maintained assets, caches and disposable working data. Resolve any [new continuing dependency](#establish-maintained-ownership-when-dependencies-appear) within authority. |
| Before cleanup or moving content | Apply the [retention and cleanup rules](#select-evidence-and-clean-up-within-authority) and relevant [directory lifecycle checks](#create-and-retire-directories-deliberately), including active-use, preservation, references and target boundaries. |
| At closeout or handoff | Complete necessary records and evidence within authority; supply [pending entries](records-and-handoff.md#when-record-writes-are-unavailable) for required unsaved updates. Link retained locations, reconcile navigation and record reduced availability and meaningful retention exceptions. Check [repository self-containment](#make-repository-records-self-contained) for affected records. |

These are event-triggered actions within one authorized batch, not separate approval stages. Reuse established source snapshots and suitable reports instead of copying the whole project on every retry. Use compact or compressed inventories when appropriate; avoid self-including archives/manifests and oversized bookkeeping. Reduce redundant storage while completing the same required tests and preserving evidence needed for their conclusions. A small ordinary check does not require a new storage framework, custom runner, per-file manifest or fresh project-wide audit.

## Select evidence and clean up within authority

| Content | Retention and disposition |
| --- | --- |
| Originals, persistent tasks, user modifications and unique data | Apply their explicit preservation/recovery requirements. Do not treat them as synthetic test scratch or infer reproducibility from the availability of source code. |
| Failed or interrupted executions | Preserve the facts, conditions, outcomes, unknowns and the scene needed to investigate. Keep relevant unique material while its role is unresolved. Record interruption honestly; it does not establish a completed test result. |
| Verification and final-delivery evidence | Preserve the necessary inputs/outputs, source association, representative supported results and distinct counterexamples that substantiate the claim. A summary alone cannot replace required original evidence. |
| Ordinary synthetic workspaces and staging | Once results are checked, necessary evidence is retained and unique data/user edits are excluded, apply authorized temporary-data cleanup. Useful failure records do not require retaining every unrelated workspace indefinitely. |
| Caches and environments | Identify the actual flow that reuses them and how they are rebuilt; merely being possibly useful is insufficient for long-term retention. Check for manual changes or unique contents before treating an environment as regenerable. |
| Packages and duplicate copies | Identify the retained source/artifact mapping and purpose. Verify claimed equivalence or recoverability before calling a copy redundant; filename, size or shared HEAD alone is insufficient. |

For `cleanup`, first identify the concrete scope, preservation rules and execution authority. Assess candidates by path, logical size, actual purpose, removal reason, retained copy or rebuild route, exceptions and evidence impact. Inspect content and consumers as needed; do not produce a full repository inventory for a narrow cleanup. A bare request without a concrete deletion boundary or applicable retention decision calls for an assessment, not speculative removal. Apply existing specific authority without repeated per-file permission; this skill, an ignore rule or a newly written policy does not create deletion authority.

Cleanup should release unnecessary storage while leaving necessary project knowledge understandable from the repository. Follow [repository self-containment](#make-repository-records-self-contained) for affected explanations, reasons, counterexamples, conditions and results. A source commit alone does not recover dirty tested source or an earlier execution. Resolve necessary document/source dependencies before deleting their only copy, within the applicable write authority. If record updates or source moves are not allowed, retain that evidence and supply the necessary [pending record content and owner](records-and-handoff.md#when-record-writes-are-unavailable); continue independent authorized cleanup. Do not use the self-containment goal to bypass a no-file-changes limit, publish private data or require a full history migration.

If disposition or authority is unresolved, retain the affected content and report the concrete missing decision. Do not weaken fidelity, evidence or original-retention requirements to save space.

Before destructive cleanup, verify resolved targets stay inside the approved boundary, check active use and link/shared targets, and establish retained exceptions and dependencies. Use literal, checked paths and one shell for filesystem operations; on Windows, do not enumerate in PowerShell and pass destructive operations to another shell. Recheck the concrete targets before deletion if they may have changed. Do not silently redirect an old result to a newer run. Unknown ownership or value calls for inspection, not a guess based on directory names.

For meaningful cleanup, retain a proportionate list of removed paths and reasons, retained exceptions and the verification performed. Keep original measurements/results and manifests honest; add a retention notice rather than rewriting historical inventories to pretend nothing was removed. A hash or inventory identifies content but cannot reconstruct deleted bytes. Report logical bytes removed separately from observed volume free-space change when measured, and qualify unestablished differences. Ordinary disposable scratch may need only a concise closeout entry, not another large audit bundle.

## Make repository records self-contained

For projects using GitHub or another repository host, maintained records must explain current rules, consequential decisions and reasons, findings, important counterexamples, verification conditions, observed results and limitations without access to the author's local directories, conversation or review ZIP. Store those explanations in their versioned owners and include the compact, shareable evidence necessary to support the claims. A local path, manifest hash or external reviewer quote alone is not the explanation. A review package is assembled from retained project content and evidence; it must not become their sole owner.

Keep small necessary examples, diffs, selected logs or manifests with the relevant record, source collection or test fixture. Label originals, excerpts, redacted copies and synthetic reproductions accurately. Preserve required originals under the product/data contract; creating a shareable excerpt does not authorize altering or deleting its source. For large, private or restricted evidence, record the protected location/access route, identity, applicable retention/availability and which conclusions cannot be independently rechecked without it. Document enough permitted facts and reasoning to understand the result. Self-containment does not authorize publishing sensitive data or claiming full reproduction from an excerpt.

At an affected record's closeout, check whether a reader with only the repository can find the governing rules, understand the choice and result, follow necessary available evidence and identify any external-access limit. Distinguish understandable project knowledge, reconstructable artifacts and independently reproducible execution; private inputs or unavailable historical state can limit the latter two even when the explanation is self-contained. Repair sole dependencies on ignored files, ephemeral links or package-only prose within authority. When access is intentionally restricted or content has been lost, disclose that limit instead of inventing a replacement observation. Check actual repository inclusion and relevant links; local existence is insufficient. GitHub Actions artifacts can expire, so their URLs are not an assumed permanent evidence store.

Distinguish recorded locally, included in version control, committed, synchronized and accessible to the intended reader. Use [Git workflow](git-workflow.md) for checkpoints and publication authority; do not push merely to satisfy this rule or claim remote availability without checking it. The check concerns changed records and their dependencies, not a fresh clone, full historical audit or new approval gate on every edit.

## Distinguish source versions from execution evidence

A source-only package can correspond to an exact commit plus its declared selection/packaging rules. Uncommitted or untracked source requires a recoverable snapshot or equivalent record of the actual bytes, including required new files. A later commit represents that earlier state only after the relevant correspondence is established. Build outputs also depend on build inputs and environment; real responses, runtime state, observations and user edits are not restored merely by checking out source.

Keep source, execution, artifact and package identities distinguishable in the existing records. Rebuilding content does not prove recovery of an earlier real execution or a byte-identical archive: compression/metadata may change. Required manifests and hashes describe the retained relationship, not a substitute backup. Use [review package rules](review-packages.md) for recipient access, requested complete contents, archive limits and extraction checks; repository self-contained explanations do not waive that package's evidence requirements.

## Established conventions behind these rules

These sources inform the distinctions; they do not prescribe one directory tree or authorize new tooling. Check the selected tool/version when configuring behavior.

The following cases illustrate why placement depends on the project's consumers and tool behavior. Consult only applicable cases; these are not required project templates or a reading checklist.

| Case and primary guidance | Implication for placement |
| --- | --- |
| [Next.js project structure](https://nextjs.org/docs/app/getting-started/project-structure) | Routing files have special meaning; `src/` is optional and related files may be colocated. Separate framework requirements from supported organization choices. |
| [PyPA src versus flat layout](https://packaging.python.org/en/latest/discussions/src-layout-vs-flat-layout/) | Layout can affect import and installation behavior. Assess those effects before relocating packages for appearance. |
| [Cargo package layout](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/guide/project-layout.html) | Source, integration tests, examples and benchmarks have recognized locations. Maintained examples/benchmarks need not live in local scratch. |
| [Turborepo repository structure](https://turborepo.dev/docs/crafting-your-repository/structuring-a-repository) | Recommended `apps/` and `packages/` organization has package boundaries. An owner can be inside a package rather than at repository root. |
| [DrivenData's Cookiecutter Data Science](https://cookiecutter-data-science.drivendata.org/#directory-structure) | This template distinguishes raw/intermediate/processed data, notebooks, models and reports. Research can be a maintained output; its exploratory status does not make it disposable. |
| [Electron app paths](https://www.electronjs.org/docs/latest/api/app#appgetpathname) | Platform data and session locations have lifecycle semantics and may be outside the checkout. Include them in the storage map without assuming they are all caches. |
| [Docker build contexts](https://docs.docker.com/build/concepts/context/#dockerignore-files) and [npm package contents](https://docs.npmjs.com/cli/v11/configuring-npm/package-json/#files) | Git tracking is not the build or distribution boundary. Inspect the selected tool/version's input, ignore and inclusion behavior. |
| [Prisma Client generation](https://www.prisma.io/docs/orm/v7/prisma-client/setup-and-configuration/generating-prisma-client) | A maintained client can be generated from schema and generator settings. Preserve that edit/regeneration relationship rather than treating output location as edit ownership. |

- [XDG Base Directory Specification](https://specifications.freedesktop.org/basedir/latest/) separates configuration, data, state, cache and runtime responsibilities for its platforms; do not transplant its paths onto every project or operating system.
- [GitHub dependency caching](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/concepts/workflows-and-actions/dependency-caching) distinguishes regenerable reuse from [workflow artifacts](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/tutorials/store-and-share-data), whose retention must be considered.
- [pytest temporary-directory guidance](https://pytest.org/en/latest/how-to/tmp_path.html) documents run retention and that an explicit `--basetemp` is cleared before a run. An output path must therefore be checked for deletion behavior, not only naming consistency.
- [GitHub source archives](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/working-with-files/using-files/downloading-source-code-archives) distinguishes commit content from mutable refs and the compressed archive representation.

# Fixed batch documents

Use this when preparing, locating or maintaining a delivery batch. Every batch uses the same separate files, regardless of size. This reference owns their layout, responsibilities and project-wide ticket-mode selection; [recording timing](records-and-handoff.md#maintain-documents-throughout-the-work) owns when updates occur.

## Use fixed paths for every batch

```text
docs/
  WORK_ITEMS.md
  batches/
    <BATCH-ID>/
      spec.md
      tickets.md
      verification.md
```

Use the existing stable batch ID, or assign one when the outcome becomes a batch. Keep that ID and directory unchanged through planning, execution, closure and later corrections. Do not move completed batches into a second archive tree. New work toward an existing batch reuses its files; a distinct selected outcome receives a new batch ID. A ticket, tool call or conversation is not automatically a new batch.

Create each file when its stage has substantive content: `spec.md` for the draft agreement, `tickets.md` for task planning, and `verification.md` for actual review/check evidence. Register each created file in the central document catalogue as well as linking the batch from WORK_ITEMS; a work-register link alone does not update the complete catalogue. Until a file exists, identify its planned destination without a broken link or a fabricated result. A small batch can have a short spec and one ticket, but cannot combine these files or embed them in WORK_ITEMS. Do not create an empty hierarchy for hypothetical future batches.

The default root is `docs/batches/`. An explicitly chosen project-wide root can replace it; declare that mapping once and retain the three filenames and separate responsibilities for every batch. Batch size, author preference or the current chat must not select a different layout. User-requested exceptions retain their actual scope and do not become an unannounced new default.

## Select one ticket mode for the project

After selection, declare the batch root and exactly one `ticket_mode` (`local` or `github-issues`) in the project's working agreement, normally `AGENTS.md`. Reuse an existing policy owner by linking it from that entrance; do not copy the setting into every batch. Include the repository identity for GitHub mode. This declaration owns project policy, not remote write permission.

Inspect current instructions, prior user choices and actual task owners first. Honor a clearly selected mode without asking again; if a prior user choice is not yet documented, save that choice within record-write authority. When no mode has been selected, explain the two arrangements, recommend one from the actual workflow, and ask the user where task content and progress should be maintained. Do not silently apply a local default. If the user explicitly delegates this choice, select within their constraints and document the rationale without another confirmation round.

| Observed working preference | Recommendation to explain |
| --- | --- |
| Repository documents are the daily planning and continuation interface | Local tickets can keep tasks beside the versioned spec, code and evidence. |
| GitHub is the desired daily task interface for triage, assignment, discussion or PR-linked tracking | GitHub Issues can own execution while repository files retain the spec and verification. |

These are recommendation criteria, not automatic selection rules. Project size, contributor/agent count, a Git remote or credentials alone do not select a mode. A concise first-choice question can be: "Where would you like to view and update task content and progress: repository tickets.md files or GitHub Issues?" Include the recommendation and its reason. If "use both" leaves the task owner unclear, explain the complementary roles below and resolve that one choice. Do not interpret silence, an unanswered question or an agent recommendation as adoption. Keep the policy unset while awaiting the answer; continue authorized spec clarification and other work that does not depend on the task-system choice, without creating a provisional competing task ledger.

If current instructions and active task owners conflict, surface the choice and proposed migration. Once selected, reuse the project policy across batches and chats. A new batch is not a reason to ask again or switch modes.

| Mode | `tickets.md` | Execution owner |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `local` | Each ticket's stable ID, contribution, criterion links, dependencies, responsibility, execution state and implementation/evidence links. Use sections in this file, not a file per ticket. | This batch's `tickets.md`. |
| `github-issues` | Stable ticket IDs and exact Issue links, plus the parent Issue link when one exists. No copied task descriptions, criteria, dependencies, assignees, checklists or progress. | The linked GitHub Issues, following [issue guidance](github-issues.md). |

Ticket mode controls where tasks are maintained, not whether GitHub can host the repository. In local mode, tracked `spec.md`, `tickets.md` and `verification.md` can be committed with code, pushed, reviewed in a PR and merged under the existing [Git authority](git-workflow.md#authority-and-project-policy). No Issue is required for that delivery route. In GitHub Issues mode, the same repository documents remain, but Issues own task content/progress and `tickets.md` supplies links. Using repository documents and GitHub together preserves one owner per fact; two manually updated task copies do not. Either mode leaves actual branch/worktree, push, PR and merge operations subject to their existing scope and authority.

The mode is uniform across the project's active batches. Changing it is an explicit project migration, with scope, old-to-new task mapping, owner cutover and repaired links. Preserve historical tasks and evidence; do not leave two editable current task owners. A temporarily unavailable GitHub service does not switch the project to local mode. Use [pending operations](records-and-handoff.md#maintain-documents-throughout-the-work) without presenting a local draft as a published Issue or a second execution ledger. Mode selection alone never authorizes remote publication.

In GitHub mode, a temporary, explicitly unpublished pending-operation section in `tickets.md` can retain a necessary create/update payload when the remote operation is unavailable or unconfirmed. This is the bounded exception to ID/link-only navigation; resolve it after checking remote state, then retain the confirmed Issue link. Do not use it as ongoing local task tracking.

## Give each file one responsibility

| Owner | Content and connections |
| --- | --- |
| WORK_ITEMS | Project-wide selection/disposition, distinct next or revisit decisions, and links to the batch spec, ticket entrance and verification when present. Keep full plans, ticket progress and batch verdicts out of this register. |
| `spec.md` | Batch outcome, scope, preserved guarantees, constraints, unresolved choices, planned acceptance criteria and applicable execution boundary. Link governing topic designs and decisions rather than copying their rules. Link the ticket entrance and, once created, verification. |
| `tickets.md` / Issues | The task information defined by the selected mode above. Every execution ticket links its specific criterion or defect basis, necessary prerequisites, implementation and actual verification evidence. |
| `verification.md` | The batch's observed checks and review results, tested spec/code/input identities, limitations and **combined acceptance verdict**. Link the exact criteria, execution tickets and implementation revisions supporting each material conclusion. Planned checks remain in the spec. |

When a criterion checks an existing design rule, keep its expected value in that rule's owner. For example, a criterion can require the rendered accessible name to equal the name defined in the linked UI contract, with a role/name assertion as the check; do not copy the literal label into the spec. The spec still supplies the relevant conditions and discriminating method. Likewise, a register entry identifies the work and its selection, then links the batch agreement; it must not reassert a normative requirement already maintained in that agreement.

The batch verdict always belongs in `verification.md`; neither the spec nor a parent Issue maintains another acceptance summary. Existing standalone reviews or dated run records remain evidence owners. Link their exact entries from verification instead of copying observations; write new batch observations here or retain a separate substantive evidence artifact when its purpose requires one. Raw outputs remain in the declared artifact store. Preserve earlier failures and correction history, with identifiable run times and versions, rather than overwriting them with the latest result. Reassess the verdict when changed scope or evidence invalidates its basis; an earlier pass does not validate a newer revision.

Use [one-owner links](documentation-structure.md#keep-one-owner-per-fact). A target in the spec is not proof of implementation. A completed ticket is not the combined batch verdict. A distinct project selection or cross-batch readiness decision can change because of that verdict, but must contribute its own information rather than repeat it.

## Make the trace navigable

Keep stable criterion and ticket IDs within the batch, for example `A1` and `<BATCH-ID>-T1`, with usable headings or anchors. References from outside the batch include its identity. Preserve established IDs and aliases when importing existing work; do not renumber for appearance.

The development entry locates a named batch through its catalogue or WORK_ITEMS; CURRENT_STATE can resume directly at its relevant section. `spec.md` links the governing decision/design sections and conditional dependencies, then the ticket entrance. Each local ticket or GitHub Issue links the precise criterion, prerequisites and actual commit/PR and evidence when available. `verification.md` connects criteria, tasks, inspected implementation and result entries, making uncovered criteria and the final verdict findable. Follow [directed reference roles](documentation-structure.md#connect-workflow-documents), not recursive traversal of every link. A planned future file is not yet a working destination.

Use current paths for navigation and exact source revisions/run entries for historical claims. GitHub Issue links must use reachable repository documents when published; expose unpublished/access-limited references and retain the local substantive content without inventing URLs or pushing outside authority. Changing a fact updates its owner and any genuinely affected dependent work, not every incoming link.

## Migrate existing batches within scope

Before moving active spec, task or verdict content, inspect current owners, local changes, incoming anchors and necessary consumers. Within authorized organization scope, move that content into the fixed destinations, account for unique meaning, and repair references to the new owner. Retain an old anchor or redirect only for an actual required consumer or explicit compatibility requirement; old filenames alone are not a reason for stubs. Reconcile the catalogue, batch entry, criterion/ticket references and applicable checks together.

Keep original discussions, captured evidence and historical snapshots intact. A later correction belongs in its appropriate current owner or a linked correction entry. Do not declare a historical batch revalidated merely because its documents were moved.

A skill update does not migrate a consuming project's files. For an existing batch whose migration is outside the request, identify its legacy owner and the outstanding migration explicitly; do not treat an exception as the new standard or silently rewrite unrelated batches. If an authorized migration must proceed in stages, document the finite remaining scope and one active owner for each affected task. No size-based permanent exceptions apply.

Validate the outcome by locating a batch from the project entry, tracing a criterion through its task to actual evidence, checking unresolved coverage and the verdict's source basis, and testing a hypothetical requirement or task-state change for redundant manual edits. Check preservation and actual path/anchor resolution as well; links alone do not prove semantic correctness.

# Debugging and learning

Read this for uncertain causes or premises, defect feedback loops, evidence applicability, misleading evaluation, or workflow retrospectives. Select the relevant sections; these decision aids are not a required sequence or form for every bug. A reported defect may need [repeatable feedback](#build-a-useful-feedback-loop); a requested retrospective or observed workflow friction uses [workflow learning](#review-workflow-friction).

## Establish the observation

Describe the expected and observed behavior using the actual input and output when available. Identify the relevant code state, configuration, environment, and execution path. Separate a report, a hypothesis, and an observed fact.

Check whether the issue lies in production behavior, test/evaluation logic, fixture data, an integration contract, or an unavailable dependency. Locate the layer before adding a workaround to an unrelated one. A failed local helper command is not automatically a product defect.

Choose scope proportionately. A reproducible local defect may have a direct small fix. Connect a design change to an intended outcome and a supported limitation or explicit benefit hypothesis. Requirements, code analysis, or a focused experiment can support restructuring without a prior production incident. Keep expected benefits distinct from verified improvements; an architecture concern alone does not justify rewriting the whole system.

## Build a useful feedback loop

For a reported defect, establish a repeatable observation that distinguishes the expected behavior from the actual symptom as early as feasible. Use a suitable existing test, command, replay, API/UI exercise or source-led artifact inspection. Confirm that the check detects the reported failure rather than an unrelated error. An assertion, exit status or explicit observation procedure can supply the verdict; not every useful reproduction is fully automated.

Shorten the loop by isolating the relevant input or path while retaining the original case, conditions and failure evidence. Prefer the smallest check that still tests the disputed behavior. Keep necessary integration and real-output checks when a smaller test cannot establish the result. Lack of a runnable reproduction does not prohibit useful source inspection or investigation; state the missing access/evidence and use permitted observations to narrow it.

Use [informative experiments](#make-an-experiment-informative) to distinguish causes, then verify the original scenario and representative affected behavior under [correction checks](#verify-the-correction-in-context). Add a regression check when it meaningfully protects the repaired behavior; do not merely mirror the implementation. Preserve necessary failure/success evidence and remove or retain temporary instrumentation according to its purpose and the project's storage rules. No fixed hypothesis count, run duration or test framework is required.

## Examine problem framing and shared causes

Treat a concrete failure as an investigation entry point, not automatically the complete problem boundary. Before selecting a remedy, examine relevant background, assumptions, requirement interpretations, shared rules and responsibility boundaries in proportion to the problem's significance. Question whether the current framing points at the right problem, rather than only finding a patch within it. Existing code or design alone does not establish that its premises are sound. A first observation can justify this examination; recurrence is not a prerequisite.

Use evidence to distinguish a local defect from a manifestation of a broader problem and choose the appropriate repair level. Do not presume a common root cause or require a full-system audit. Stop expanding when the evidence supports the scoped choice; identify any remaining unknown that could change it. Questioning an explicit requirement does not authorize changing it; preserve the decision and execution boundaries in [Fit the actual task](../SKILL.md#fit-the-actual-task).

When related failures recur across fixes, compare the affected paths before adding another exception. Identify supported operations that share the disputed rule, what each stage decides, which state or representation it uses, and whether an accepted step has a valid continuation. Explain why prior changes and checks missed the behavior. Distinguish a later regression, an inherited defect, a capability gap and insufficient earlier acceptance evidence; recurrence alone does not prove a shared architectural cause.

Different stages may legitimately use different state, estimates or criteria. Require clear purposes and compatible transitions, not identical values or a mandatory common helper. A cheaper or smaller representation does not by itself preserve meaning or dependencies. Compare corrections to the existing flow with changes to shared responsibility when evidence supports them; neither a local patch nor restructuring is inherently the right remedy.

## Trace the handoff and preserve useful work

Follow the relevant input, intermediate result, and actual saved or delivered output. Find the last stage evidenced to satisfy the disputed requirement and the first observed loss or error. Inspect the boundary between them: an adapter, eligibility decision, adoption step, persistence operation, or consumer may discard valid upstream work. Missing intermediate evidence leaves that boundary uncertain; do not invent a successful stage.

Separate an operation's effect, its returned response and final delivery. A mutation may commit before response formatting, field selection or transport fails; an error reply is not proof of rollback. Before replaying a potentially mutating operation, use available receipts, exact revision/operation identity or saved state to establish what took effect. Unknown outcomes need reconciliation rather than blind replay. When prepared content or rejected arguments are available, reuse valid work while correcting metadata or other faults instead of regenerating it unnecessarily; its availability alone does not certify correctness.

Retain usable artifacts, their input/revision identity, verified scope, and remaining issues. Before continuing from or adopting them, check authority, compatibility, and true dependencies. Independent valid parts may survive an unrelated failure; a dependent group may need to change together. Newest output or the fewest reported issues does not establish the best candidate, and local verification does not approve the whole composition.

Example: a prepared report contains forty required records, while the saved report contains thirty-nine. Compare preparation and persistence before repeating preparation. Preserve the prepared result; verify the corrected saved artifact and its actual export.

## Preserve semantics and evidence scope

Establish the contract's meanings for relevant missing, null/unknown, empty, zero, false, and default values. Trace those meanings through validation, transformation, storage, and presentation. A truthiness fallback can turn an explicit empty selection into all items or a valid zero into a default. A display fallback does not establish that unknown source data is known. Check the affected end-to-end path and meaningful valid/invalid cases; do not impose different semantics where the contract treats values equivalently.

Evidence supports the subject and conditions actually observed. Identify the relevant content or fields, dependencies, revision, inputs, and environment before applying a previous result to changed work. A version increment or bookkeeping change may leave an observation applicable; unchanged text alone may not preserve an ordering, permission, or calculation claim. Reuse needs an established mapping to the current subject. Missing scope or changed dependencies require further evidence or an explicit unresolved claim.

Example: changing a report's export timestamp can leave a check of its line amounts applicable. Changing currency or the included lines can invalidate its total even if the displayed total is unchanged. A field observation, a candidate review, and approval of a final composed report have different scopes.

## Make an experiment informative

Identify the uncertainty the next action will resolve. Use the smallest meaningful reproduction or intervention that distinguishes plausible causes. A code edit is one option; inspecting a saved payload, tracing a path, comparing outputs, or independently reading a source may be more informative.

For consequential or costly experiments, establish proportionate question, acceptance, observation and closure criteria before execution, including relevant stopping and recovery limits. Ending a bounded attempt is distinct from answering its original question: a blocked or inconclusive run can close honestly while the intended comparison remains unresolved. State the evidence gap and next discriminating option without declaring an untested feature effective or ineffective, automatically queuing another run, or continuing until a preferred answer wins. This does not require a plan template or a fixed attempt limit for every ordinary fix.

Keep relevant variables stable and identify what changed. Use the [batch protocol](artifacts-and-storage.md#manage-each-batch-from-creation-to-closeout) to associate each execution with its actual inputs, source, command and outputs before interpreting it; filenames and timestamps alone do not establish that mapping. Check that the intended version ran, the change reached the relevant path, and the observation could detect its effect. Reuse saved evidence when it answers the question; rerunning an expensive workflow should resolve an actual remaining uncertainty within authorized scope.

For quality or efficiency comparisons, align the input, workload, code/configuration, evaluator, and measured stages as relevant. Retain failed outcomes, unknown costs and necessary diagnostic evidence under the [retention rules](artifacts-and-storage.md#select-evidence-and-clean-up-within-authority). Fewer requests alone does not establish lower total cost; changed model responses or input populations can confound attribution to a code change. State the supported comparison and its limits.

For consequential optimizations, include relevant end-to-end overhead and tradeoffs such as rereading, coordination, recovery and maintenance. A smaller intermediate result, more passing tests or repaired defects does not by itself establish useful net benefit. Capacity, quality, autonomy or user effort may matter even without shorter-task savings. Correct concrete obstacles to the question rather than prebuilding speculative infrastructure to justify a feature. When evidence warrants simplification or removal, explain any change needed to an agreed constraint and implement only within applicable authorization; not every routine change needs a quantitative benefit study.

Classify the result as supporting, contradicting, or leaving a hypothesis unresolved. No observed improvement may reflect a weak intervention, a masked effect, measurement error, or the wrong cause. It does not by itself establish falsification or locate an architectural defect.

When attempts repeat without new information, summarize what they establish and choose a different discriminating method. State the actual blocker if progress needs missing information or an external change. Avoid silently recycling equivalent patches or abandoning work at an invented universal retry limit.

## Check the meaning of measurements

Before a metric determines success or failure, understand:

- Which inputs, outputs, units, identifiers, and populations it actually compares.
- Whether the reference is independent enough to detect the relevant defect.
- How missing, empty, skipped, failed, or unknown results affect the numerator and denominator.
- Whether expected items absent from the output can be detected, using requirements or an appropriate independent inventory rather than only surviving output. Distinguish a real omission from an allowed alternate representation or justified exclusion.
- Whether matching labels or internal IDs establish the user-visible property being claimed.
- Whether the code/input identity belongs to the reported run, including uncommitted changes.

Select relevant questions rather than writing a measurement form for every test. Use a known failing case and a valid control when they help show that a changed evaluator distinguishes outcomes. Preserve original scores and explain any scoring change; identify recomputation or replay separately from a new application run.

Distinguish illustrative examples from authoritative fixtures and explicit acceptance requirements. A user-approved or AI-authored sample may demonstrate acceptable form without certifying every value or setting a quality ceiling. Its incidental mistakes are not inherited requirements; use the task's authoritative source and agreed criteria, and surface material conflicts rather than silently discarding an explicit requirement. This adds no routine independent-approval stage.

Example: a sender reports 100% because every request returned HTTP 200. The receiver's result body says no records were accepted. Inspect the receiver contract and saved outputs, determine why records are rejected, and make the reported status reflect acceptance. A unit test of the sender's request count cannot establish delivery.

Example: a patch changes a prompt, but the output is unchanged. Confirm the modified prompt was sent, relevant candidates were eligible, and the comparison observes the intended property before drawing a conclusion about the prompt hypothesis.

## Establish whether a mechanism contributed

For the claim under investigation, distinguish whether a capability is available, invoked, executed, returned a result, had that result consumed, and affected the delivered outcome. Use the relevant trace, payload, or artifact; a configured flag or a callable tool is insufficient evidence of use. Successful use can still yield no quality benefit.

Distinguish a controlled exercise of a mechanism from spontaneous use in ordinary work; they answer different questions, and neither makes use mandatory on every task. A failure before invocation excludes that unexecuted transition as its direct cause, but does not exonerate changed prompts, schemas or shared paths already in effect. Inspect the relevant trace and preserve uncertainty about causality.

Example: a retry feature exists and is enabled, but a smoke test encounters no failure. That run establishes the successful path only. To assess recovery, exercise a representative failure within authorized scope and inspect the resulting behavior. Record an unexercised path as unverified, rather than ineffective or proven.

## Verify the correction in context

Check the original failure and representative supported behaviors that depend on the changed responsibility. Choose cases that distinguish meaningful conditions, action order or transitions; do not enumerate every combination. Derive expected outcomes from requirements or independent evidence rather than calculating them with the same decision logic under test. A successful scripted path may exercise only one way through the feature. Exercise the connected workflow and actual output when unit checks do not establish the affected user result, including relevant interruption or failure behavior. Reuse evidence whose applicability is established and state what remains unchecked.

Do not weaken acceptance to make a failing implementation pass. If the test or requirement interpretation was wrong, use the authoritative requirement and observed evidence to explain and verify its correction. A temporary containment measure should retain the unresolved root cause in the record.

Independent review can help with consequential or ambiguous changes when available and authorized. Supply the task, requirements, actual revision/artifacts, and raw relevant evidence. For an initial independent diagnosis, avoid supplying the expected finding or preferred explanation. Verify review findings against the current files and record what was actually covered; review does not substitute for the missing runtime evidence.

## Turn review into a decision

Use [Review and reconciliation](review.md) for the shared process across current-conversation reviews, authorized subagent reviews, external review handoffs, returned feedback, document adoption and improvement batches. It governs assessing claims, selecting dispositions and record authority. The observation and experiment guidance here supplies methods for checking evidence; it does not authorize changes to project records, new requirements or implementation of a finding.

Assess review findings against the current objective, implementation, and evidence. Identify which findings change the current decision or prevent the intended result, which need investigation, and which can be recorded for later consideration. A reviewer or AI can discover a valid need; a finding is not automatically a requirement or an addition to the current work.

Use [the review closeout rules](review.md#improvement-batches-and-closeout) to identify readiness, blockers and deferred findings, and [Fit the actual task](../SKILL.md#fit-the-actual-task) for material choices that need the user. Once the evidence supports a next step within a selected or delegated approach, carry out authorized work rather than repeatedly expanding the design. Discussion and review retain their requested mode. Do not require every hypothetical counterexample to be eliminated or reopen settled choices merely because another alternative exists; use changed requirements, new evidence or a material limitation to justify reconsideration.

## Review workflow friction

Use `retro`, "review this workflow" or equivalent requests to examine the specified session or batch; infer the current one when clear. During ordinary delivery, also notice consequential or repeated friction and preserve useful lessons without requiring a retrospective after every ticket. Read available primary session evidence and affected tools/documents. Distinguish observed time, retries, repeated retrieval or user interventions from estimates and inferred causes.

Look for a concrete cause and a proportionate improvement: missing navigation, scattered or contradictory guidance, a broken or unused existing check, slow defect feedback, redundant tool calls, or unavailable necessary information. Inspect existing scripts/checks and their actual use before proposing replacements. A deterministic check can suit a mechanical error; a judgment problem may need a clearer example or rule. Use [agent-readable guidance](documentation-structure.md#write-guidance-for-agents) for instruction changes. More rules, agents or documentation are not improvement evidence by themselves.

For each consequential candidate, preserve the observation and source, causal uncertainty, proposed intervention, expected benefit and what later result would support or reject it. Rank by supported impact and cost. Record the lesson in its existing project discussion/review/learning owner and connect outstanding work to the register where useful. Apply improvements within existing implementation authority; a retrospective-only request produces assessment and documents. Updating a general skill, changing broader settings or obtaining new access requires its applicable scope rather than following automatically from one project's experience.

When an improvement is implemented, verify its direct effect and assess later representative work where evidence is available. Retain unsuccessful attempts and limits under [reusable learning](#preserve-reusable-learning). A smaller prompt or passing unit check alone does not establish lower whole-task cost or better delivery. Stop when the requested retrospective has a supported assessment and useful next action; it need not become another delivery gate.

## Preserve reusable learning

Use [Track discoveries](records-and-handoff.md#track-discoveries-without-expanding-the-current-work) for recording all new findings and decisions, exact owner locations and pending entries when writes are unauthorized. [Review and reconciliation](review.md#adoption-and-documentation) governs adoption; recording a tentative or unadopted conclusion does not turn it into effective requirements, architecture/design decisions or operating instructions. Investigation evidence can include:

> Problem or hypothesis; relevant input/code identity; intervention and conditions; actual outcome; evidence location; conclusion with its limits; unresolved next question.

Record meaningful unsuccessful attempts as well as successes. Distinguish an unexecuted proposal, a configuration that was present but unused, a saved-response replay, and a new real execution. Preserve required originals and earlier results under the [storage policy](artifacts-and-storage.md#select-evidence-and-clean-up-within-authority); [repository records](artifacts-and-storage.md#make-repository-records-self-contained) must retain the reasoning and necessary shareable evidence, not only a local batch path.

Promote a finding to a reusable lesson only when it can guide another decision. Include its applicability and counterexamples, link the supporting record, and revise it as evidence changes. Consult relevant lessons when useful; routine development does not require reading all experiments or old conversations.

# Subagent delegation

Read this when deciding whether to delegate or when coordinating subagent work. Work directly by default. Use subagents only when the user explicitly requests or authorizes them. Once authorized, do not ask for repeated approval within that scope. Apply higher-priority instructions and environment restrictions; if subagents are unavailable or prohibited, continue with permitted methods and do not imply that independent delegation occurred. A subagent inherits the task's mode, scope, write limits, budgets and external-action restrictions. Delegation does not expand them.

## Choose a useful assignment

When the user has explicitly requested or authorized subagents, delegate when a clear contribution can improve evidence, completion time or the reliability of a handoff enough to outweigh setup, context transfer and integration costs. Suitable work may proceed independently or provide a useful second perspective after an earlier step. Sequential delegation can be useful; parallel execution is not required. Handle small edits and tightly coupled decisions directly when delegation would mostly duplicate work or create coordination overhead.

| Work | Useful contribution |
| --- | --- |
| Code and evidence investigation | Trace a bounded call or data path, check a specific claim, or produce a discriminating local reproduction with source references. |
| Design assessment | Evaluate meaningful alternatives, state transitions, responsibility boundaries or recovery behavior against the actual requirements. |
| Discussion synthesis | Extract attributed positions, known times, corrections and open questions from supplied conversations or reports, preserving sources and uncertainty. |
| Implementation | Deliver an authorized component or coherent change with clear interfaces, file ownership and relevant checks. |
| Verification and review | Inspect representative requirements and transitions, run permitted checks, or compare actual saved/reopened/exported results with their sources. |
| Handoff reading | Use maintained documents and necessary sources to identify the intended work, adopted decisions, open questions and acceptance conditions. |

These are possible assignments, not a fixed team or required sequence. Use the project's actual needs to choose the number and timing of agents. An additional review should answer a material unresolved question, not automatically follow every earlier review.

## Give enough context and a clear boundary

Provide a concise assignment containing:

- The question or deliverable and its purpose in the current task.
- Relevant user requirements, adopted decisions, known open choices and source locations. Identify the actual revision or working-tree state when it affects the conclusion.
- The mode and allowed actions, including whether the assignment is read-only, may create isolated verification artifacts, or may modify designated files. Carry through limits on model calls, external changes and experiments.
- File or artifact responsibility, shared dependencies and the boundary for requesting coordination. Define a useful stopping condition and any applicable resource limit.
- The expected evidence: concrete references, actual changes and checks, results, limitations and remaining decisions. Do not prescribe a finding count or a favorable conclusion.

Provide the minimum sufficient context with access to necessary original evidence. For an independent first diagnosis, avoid giving the preferred answer or the main conversation's unverified explanation. For reconciliation, provide the disputed review and label the assignment as checking that claim. Do not withhold relevant requirements or contrary evidence to create apparent independence.

When testing document- or skill-guided behavior, identify the fixture's project, allowed sources, output boundary and actual skill revision. Use a fresh context when available; verify and disclose inherited workspace instructions rather than equating a fresh conversation with a clean environment. Host-project facts must not become facts about a separate fixture. Label logical scenario exclusion separately from removal of background. For version comparisons, keep the case, model and evaluation criteria fixed, preserve first responses, and distinguish unaided selection from directed-reading or correction trials. Judge semantic outcomes and unnecessary work, not prescribed wording or reference counts. Comparison controls belong in the evaluation setup, not in every ordinary delegation.

## Coordinate shared work

Assign one writer or integrator at a time for overlapping files and shared contracts, indexes or state. Multiple agents may edit disjoint assigned areas when the task permits it; the main conversation need not type every change. A source-extraction or review assignment does not independently adopt proposals or rewrite effective specifications. A documentation writer may make the explicitly assigned changes within the task's document-write authority.

Make shared interface assumptions visible before parallel implementation. Use the agreed [ticket dependencies and responsibilities](implementation.md#turn-a-spec-into-tickets) to assign ready work and keep tightly coupled changes together. If work needs an overlapping edit, coordinate the handoff or revise ownership rather than overwriting another agent's work. Give mutable test artifacts distinct locations when needed, and do not run conflicting checks against shared state. Follow [Git workflow](git-workflow.md) for checkout isolation and integration; delegation does not require a new worktree or change its authorization rules.

Before dispatch, establish the assignment's claim/owner, settled prerequisites and integration target in the existing work record. Avoid duplicate dispatch of the same work. Give each implementer the applicable spec, relevant decisions and current source state, with pointers to necessary detail instead of requiring the entire conversation. As results arrive, reconcile shared changes and newly ready dependencies through [the batch loop](implementation.md#deliver-the-agreed-batch); there is no mandatory agent per ticket or separate merger role.

When using [task worktrees](git-workflow.md#choose-and-close-branches-and-worktrees), include the exact checkout, branch, source basis and expected returned commit/diff plus checks. Reconcile dependent work onto its actual prerequisite before dispatch. For [GitHub tickets](github-issues.md#create-useful-issues-and-relationships), link the execution claim to the issue without pretending a subagent is a GitHub account. The main agent coordinates issue updates and integration; child agents publish or merge only when those operations are explicitly within their assignments.

Continue useful independent work while assignments run. Pass on material scope changes or new user instructions, and stop or redirect affected assignments when necessary. Preserve useful partial results. Do not report the overall task complete while a required assignment or integration check is still unresolved; unrelated discoveries remain subject to the current scope.

## Integrate evidence and results

Ask agents to return their conclusion or deliverable, concrete source/artifact references, the state inspected or changed, checks actually performed and their results, uncertainty and unresolved work. Distinguish original observations from supplied logs and proposed checks. Use [Review and reconciliation](review.md#reconcile-findings-with-evidence) for returned findings.

Treat a returned implementation as ready for integration only when its prerequisites and source basis remain applicable. If the integration target changed, identify affected assumptions and reconcile them without discarding unrelated work. Keep implementation complete, integrated and accepted distinguishable in the existing task representation; a delegated success report does not close the whole batch.

The main agent retains responsibility for [the whole agreed batch](implementation.md#deliver-the-agreed-batch), consequential choices, integration and final reporting. Route supported scoped review findings back to implementation and verification, and continue ready work until integrated acceptance or a specific unresolved blocker. The main agent coordinates these transitions without making the user relay assignments or findings. Check high-impact claims, source applicability and shared boundaries proportionately. Reuse adequate evidence instead of automatically repeating every delegated investigation; rerun checks where integration, changed inputs or unresolved concerns justify it. Inspect the resulting combined state rather than treating separate passing reports as proof that it works together.

Resolve disagreements by identifying the disputed premise and seeking the smallest useful permitted check or the applicable user decision. Neither majority agreement nor the main conversation's authorship establishes correctness. Retain substantive unresolved differences with their evidence. Within record-write authority, integrate findings and changes into the existing discussion, design, implementation and evidence owners; do not create competing official records for each agent. Label proposed, adopted, implemented and verified outcomes accurately, including any limits of the delegation itself.
