## Orient from current evidence

For `orient` or a request to identify the next work, use the [target rule](../SKILL.md#use-a-short-work-entry) to find the actual project/skill entry. CURRENT_STATE locates interaction continuity; PHASE_PLAN and the [work register](records-and-handoff.md#maintain-the-project-work-register) supply direction and candidates. Reconcile them with the request and observable working state, including uncommitted changes. Scan consequential outstanding work across topics before selecting; the latest topic or completed increment alone does not determine the next step. For a known task or simple "continue", use [task-based reading](documentation-structure.md#read-by-task-and-follow-dependencies) and the recorded activity instead of reopening selection. Do not read every historical source or assume an uninspected default path exists.

When the register is absent, incomplete or stale, use the declared finding, design, verification and proposal owners to recover a bounded view of consequential outstanding work. State coverage limits and material conflicts instead of treating missing entries as no remaining problems. Reconcile necessary documents and navigation under [automatic documentation](records-and-handoff.md#maintain-documents-throughout-the-work), preserving proposal status. Explicit write restrictions use pending content.

Report what is actually in place, the verification level and limits, effective scope/decisions, meaningful unresolved issues, reusable evidence and the next useful action. Cite relevant item IDs or exact owner sections and explain the selection and important deferrals using [increment selection](#choose-a-coherent-increment). Identify missing decisions, evidence or authority precisely. A deferred improvement is not automatically a blocker, and old budgets, commands or permissions are not current authorization.

Orientation alone finishes with this assessment and necessary document updates. If the user also requested and authorized further work, continue it without requiring a second "orient" approval or a new chat; retain the material decision boundary. Reading readiness does not authorize tests, provider calls or recovery actions outside the task. Use [task entry points](#enter-at-the-relevant-point) below for the selected continuation.

## Enter at the relevant point

| Situation | Start with |
| --- | --- |
| New project | Product outcome, constraints and necessary architecture/contracts; select the first complete, verifiable path. Establish the [core development records](documentation-structure.md#establish-the-development-entry) and storage from the start within write authority. Detail only what the upcoming work requires, not every future feature. |
| Substantial new capability or changed method | Actual baseline, proposed behavior and preserved guarantees; resolve material choices before dependent implementation. |
| Small repair within a selected method | Existing specification and a discriminating regression case. A concise scope and check can suffice without a new specification file or full design cycle. |
| Unknown cause or feasibility | A bounded question, permitted investigation, observations that would change the decision and stopping conditions. Use [experiments](debugging-and-learning.md) as needed; exploratory results do not adopt a design. |
| Discussion, planning or standalone review | The requested decision, plan or assurance result and necessary documentation. Continue further work only within its applicable authorization. Explicit write limits use pending records. |
| Document or maintenance work | The affected meaning, usability or maintenance outcome and proportionate checks; do not invent a UI milestone. |

## Keep the project direction

Organize phases around useful, observable outcomes for the user or agent. An increment is a coherent piece of work; a phase may span several increments and technical layers. A review batch groups related proposed work: when selected, it may become increments within existing phases, a standalone task, or a new phase when useful. A version milestone marks significant saved or delivered work and need not correspond one-to-one to a phase or batch. Select boundaries from the task; there is no fixed phase count or required backend/frontend/testing sequence. Include the verification and relevant failure behavior needed to establish each outcome.

Keep the current and next phases concrete enough to guide execution. For distant phases, preserve intended outcomes, likely dependencies and unresolved choices without speculative task lists or commitments. PHASE_PLAN is the roadmap: it links relevant work-register IDs and explains their relationship to phase outcomes. The register owns item dispositions, while detailed owners retain explanations and evidence. Keep unselected discoveries visible under [Track discoveries](records-and-handoff.md#track-discoveries-without-expanding-the-current-work).

When starting an increment or resuming work, reconcile current human instructions, effective product requirements, the relevant phase, outstanding work, actual state and available evidence before selecting the next action. Use the connection **phase outcome -> relevant work items -> justified increment -> verification -> reassessed readiness**. Recent conversation or the latest edited list of details alone is not a sufficient direction record.

Select the next result from the effective product goal and adopted scope, not simply the most recent finding. A standalone task need not create a phase. Keep durable direction under [phase records](records-and-handoff.md#maintain-a-rolling-phase-plan); CURRENT_STATE identifies the selected interaction focus and resume activity, with progress and readiness at their substantive owners.

## Turn a spec into tickets

For `tickets`, work splitting or an authorized batch needing a plan, use the adopted spec and actual project state. Follow [spec clarification](discussion-and-design.md#clarify-and-prepare-a-spec) where material choices remain open. Group decisions that can usefully be discussed together before implementation, and keep uncertain dependent work visibly blocked.

Each ticket identifies a verifiable contribution to the selected outcome. Link its purpose/spec and existing completion criteria; write task-specific prerequisites, responsible implementer or role, shared interface/file ownership and necessary checks in the [project-selected execution owner](batch-documents.md#select-one-ticket-mode-for-the-project). Local tickets live in the batch's separate `tickets.md`; GitHub mode uses that file only for ID/Issue navigation and keeps execution details in Issues. Apply [one-owner maintenance](documentation-structure.md#keep-one-owner-per-fact) instead of copying acceptance text or status. Reuse existing IDs. A single ticket still uses the fixed layout. For GitHub, follow [issue ownership and relationships](github-issues.md); remote creation or publication needs its applicable authority.

In the existing task representation, distinguish work ready to start, active work, a specific blocker, implementation awaiting integration/acceptance, and accepted work. These are useful distinctions rather than mandatory status labels. Identify the actual result and evidence when reporting progress. Keep fine-grained execution progress in the batch owner; the project work register owns the broader item's current disposition.

Prefer useful end-to-end slices for features. Group tightly coupled fixes around the shared responsibility they repair. A necessary investigation, refactor or integration check can have its own verifiable ticket. Choose size by coherent purpose, dependencies and reviewability. Include the integration and whole-spec acceptance work so individual ticket passes can be checked against the combined result.

Order work by real dependencies. Identify ready tickets, opportunities for independent work, shared interfaces that must settle first and overlapping files needing one writer or integrator. Task decomposition can support direct or delegated execution. Use [delegation](delegation.md) only within its applicable authorization and environment rules. Update dependencies when discoveries change the plan and explain material changes to the agreed outcome or method.

Keep the spec and task plan connected through the [batch work owner](records-and-handoff.md#record-the-increment-basis-and-task-owner). A ticket-planning request finishes with that plan and its unresolved decisions. When implementation is already authorized, continue into the ready work without asking the user to invoke another entry.

## Deliver the agreed batch

The main agent owns the selected outcome from implementation through testing, review, corrections, integration, documentation and acceptance. A request to implement an agreed spec covers its selected tickets and the scoped work needed to meet that spec. Separate execution restrictions, budgets, external actions and material human decisions still apply. A batch may span several increments or sessions while retaining its scope and integrated acceptance condition.

Manage the following loop using the batch's existing task owner. For GitHub-backed work, maintain [issue progress](github-issues.md#maintain-progress-during-execution) at meaningful transitions and follow [the repository execution agreement](git-workflow.md#authority-and-project-policy) for branches, worktrees and publication:

1. **Select ready work.** Reconcile prerequisites and the actual spec/source/evidence basis, including the [daily document check](records-and-handoff.md#keep-documents-current-during-daily-work); claim responsibility before assigning work. Settle shared interface assumptions and coordinate overlapping files through one writer/integrator. Keep tightly coupled changes together; use authorized delegation or checkout isolation where their benefit exceeds coordination cost. A blocked ticket leaves independent authorized work available.
2. **Implement and check.** Build the verifiable contribution, using a [useful feedback loop](debugging-and-learning.md#build-a-useful-feedback-loop) for defects. Preserve its changed-state identity, actual checks and unresolved limits. Implementation completion is not yet proof of integrated acceptance.
3. **Integrate.** Inspect the actual combined files/artifacts and changed dependencies under [Git integration](git-workflow.md#integrate-and-recover-deliberately). Reconcile interfaces and run the checks needed for shared behavior. Separate passing ticket reports do not establish that they work together.
4. **Review and correct.** Cover [spec and engineering concerns](review.md#review-spec-and-engineering-concerns), including affected current claims in unchanged documentation. Apply [convergence](#resolve-differences-and-converge): repair supported requirements violations, stale in-scope descriptions and introduced regressions, add discriminating checks where needed and recheck affected integrated behavior. Required corrections stay within this batch; separate improvements receive a documented disposition. Return material changes of requirement/design for their applicable decision unless delegated.
5. **Accept and deliver.** Check the whole selected spec, including required saved, reopened or delivered results. Complete the [daily document check](records-and-handoff.md#keep-documents-current-during-daily-work) with a brief impact/evidence note in the existing verification owner, then complete [authorized delivery](#explain-delivery-and-prepare-a-pr). Passing code or link checks cannot close a batch with supported in-scope stale claims left unresolved. A required unmet condition remains unfinished.

Reassess dependencies, evidence and risks after meaningful changes, and continue ready work without another user prompt. Keep the user informed at useful checkpoints; they should not relay assignments or review findings. Delegation and independent review follow their existing authority and environment rules. Otherwise perform the work directly and report the method accurately. Standalone review retains its assessment/documentation scope.

Stop when scoped acceptance has sufficient evidence and no supported blocker remains, or identify a specific remaining decision, permission, unavailable capability or external blocker after completing independent authorized work. Honor user Stop and resource bounds. Repeat or broaden checks only when changes, failures or unresolved concerns justify them. If consequential workflow friction appears, use [retrospective learning](debugging-and-learning.md#review-workflow-friction) proportionately without making it a new mandatory delivery gate.

## Explain delivery and prepare a PR

Lead with the concrete problem and resulting behavior, using a before/after example when useful. Supply evidence that supports the result, the actual version/artifacts checked and meaningful unverified scope. Explain material impact on callers, data, configuration or recovery when applicable. A small documentation change can use a short explanation; a diagram, long risk template or PR is not mandatory for every batch.

For a requested PR, use the repository's template and policy, with a concise problem/result summary, relevant evidence and integration/recovery considerations. Check that the title and body describe the final changes, not abandoned approaches. Link the spec or work item and useful verification rather than copying their full histories. Clarify requested scope from context: drafting PR text, creating a remote PR and publishing a branch have different effects. Perform supporting Git actions under [existing authority](git-workflow.md#authority-and-project-policy); prepare the concrete result before asking for any genuinely missing publication approval.

Ordinary local delivery uses the same explanation and necessary documentation without implying remote publication. Report remaining blockers or next useful work according to actual readiness; do not present a new proposal stage as the continuation of completed work unless it is needed.

For remote delivery, follow [push, review and merge](git-workflow.md#publish-review-and-merge-the-selected-result) through the authorized endpoint. Link [issue completion](github-issues.md#connect-prs-and-close-against-evidence) to the actual acceptance condition, including any required post-merge work; opening a PR alone does not establish whole-batch acceptance.

## Choose a coherent increment

For open-ended improvement of an existing project, prioritize consequential defects, then capability gaps in the intended user flow, then valuable new functions. This is a revisable priority, not a requirement to clear every defect first. Explicit feature requests and new projects follow their own objectives and necessary dependencies.

Before recommending the next increment, compare the meaningful candidates from the work register by product impact, evidence strength, dependencies, readiness, cost and the user's objective. Follow evidence for consequential items even when they belong to another topic or phase. State why the recommended work takes priority and why important alternatives can wait, with their revisit conditions. Do not substitute bug counts, age, an old plan's order or the most recently discussed feature for this assessment. Reuse an already-selected scope unless new evidence or instructions change its basis; routine steps within it need no repeated project-wide ranking.

Before proposing costly live validation or operations, assess known defects and gaps that could invalidate the result, defeat required behavior or cause avoidable expense. Prefer the relevant repair or cheaper discriminating check first when existing evidence supports it. If live work is needed first, identify the question it can resolve, why available lower-cost evidence is insufficient, and how the remaining defects affect interpretation. A phase named for a real-world outcome does not itself justify performing that operation next. This assessment neither requires eliminating every bug nor grants execution authority.

Actively discover needs and improvements from users, reviewers, agent analysis, and tests. Explain the underlying problem and expected value without prematurely fixing the solution. Select work by relevance, value, dependencies, and current authorization; the user need not enumerate every improvement. Preserve useful other findings for later consideration instead of automatically adding them to the current increment.

Define each work increment by the authorized capability or user outcome, its supported conditions, and observable completion criteria, not file count or patch size. Resolve and record the material rules needed for that work under [Record decisions before dependent work](records-and-handoff.md#record-decisions-before-dependent-work), without waiting for a complete project-wide specification. Reported failures supply evidence and regression cases, not automatically all acceptance criteria. Keep the outcome focused while allowing the implementation depth needed to satisfy it; a narrow repair can be small, and a capability repair can span modules or require reconstruction. Do not exclude behavior required by that outcome merely because it was absent from the bug list or labeled an edge case. Make material scope changes explicit.

The plan reflects current knowledge. Distinguish record maintenance from changes to delivery commitments: a correction to evidence, implementation detail, confirmed defect, candidate improvement and adopted scope change have different effects. Adding or editing text does not itself create a new requirement or acceptance condition. Before including newly discovered work in the current phase, explain whether it is necessary for the adopted outcome, a supported blocker to correct or safe continuation, or an independently useful improvement. Preserve the latter for separate selection unless already authorized and selected as part of this phase; its presence in a detailed document is not an instruction to execute it.

Actively discover necessary capabilities and test important assumptions; omission from the plan is not a reason to reject work needed for the intended outcome. Within authorized scope, add necessary implementation detail without per-detail approval. Deepen or change implementation, or revise phase structure when evidence justifies it, while applying [Fit the actual task](../SKILL.md#fit-the-actual-task) to material choices and changes to agreed outcomes or constraints. Record adopted revisions and keep the effective plan consistent with selected work; preserve unselected ideas without making each one a development commitment.

Follow the connected activities below, returning to the responsible activity when evidence changes the basis. They are not mandatory separate documents, chats or approval gates.

| Activity | Result and next action |
| --- | --- |
| Orient and select | Establish the [specification basis](#establish-the-specification-basis), useful outcome, scope, preserved guarantees and observable completion conditions. Proceed when material choices are settled or delegated. |
| Prepare | Record the necessary design and [connect tasks to requirements](#connect-tasks-implementation-and-evidence). Identify real dependencies and integration order without prescribing every coding detail. |
| Implement and verify | Build a working path and exercise the affected behavior. Diagnose failures and make necessary repairs within scope; reconcile material discoveries with the design and task owner. |
| Resolve and accept | Apply [convergence](#resolve-differences-and-converge) to deviations and new findings. Check actual coverage of the adopted outcome, rather than only task completion or the latest patch. |
| Save and deliver | Finish affected records, retained evidence, artifact closeout and applicable Git/delivery work. Where necessary record writes are unavailable, [provide ready-to-save pending entries and exact owners](records-and-handoff.md#when-record-writes-are-unavailable). State actual readiness and unchecked scope. |
| Continue | Reconcile changed work items and readiness, then assess [phase completion](#close-or-revise-a-phase) and next-work selection. Resume applicable already-authorized work; otherwise provide the justified next decision. |

Complete each authorized implementation increment with its necessary repairs, proportionate review, relevant verification and affected records together, then continue the [selected batch](#deliver-the-agreed-batch). Use a handoff, independent reviewer or further measurement when it addresses a concrete need. Apply the task's write, execution and external-action limits and pause material choices under [Fit the actual task](../SKILL.md#fit-the-actual-task).

For substantial features, organize useful increments around a user completing a task. When the core outcome is unproven, start with the smallest complete, observable input-to-output path within the selected design and accepted quality constraints. Add capabilities on top of a working, integrated product; preserve usable outcomes and verify each increment before treating it as the next baseline. Necessary refactoring can change internals, but unfinished complexity or a smaller demonstration does not replace required delivery. Include relevant failure and recovery behavior; this selects no universal backend-first order.

For exploratory or user-facing work, provide an early usable result or preview at a useful checkpoint. Incorporate feedback into the next increment and update agreed requirements when the user changes direction. Continue independent authorized work while feedback is pending; checkpoints do not create an approval requirement.

Consider the quality concerns introduced by the change, such as usability and accessibility, security and privacy, performance and cost, compatibility, and data integrity. For release or migration work, consider operational visibility and recovery. Apply only the relevant checks or specialist guidance. Choose task splitting, TDD, worktrees and independent review when they add value and fit the current scope and environment.

For new projects or new data responsibilities, establish the [storage policy](artifacts-and-storage.md#plan-storage-when-the-project-starts) before dependent generation. Use the [batch protocol](artifacts-and-storage.md#manage-each-batch-from-creation-to-closeout) for verification outputs and closeout within the same increment; settled storage rules need no separate planning or approval stage.

## Establish the specification basis

Before dependent implementation, distinguish three facts in the [increment's existing work owner](records-and-handoff.md#record-the-increment-basis-and-task-owner):

- **Reference baseline:** the relevant existing requirement, topic design and shared-contract revisions, together with the actual source/work state used for comparison. The intended baseline and implemented behavior may already differ.
- **Adopted target:** this increment's selected changes, preserved guarantees, scope and completion conditions, with decision status and applicable authority. An adopted target can precede implementation; label that state.
- **Actual readiness:** what is implemented, verified or unresolved, tied to the code state and evidence actually examined. Record partial coverage and unknowns rather than inferring completion from adoption.

Reuse existing records and identifiers. Requirements must describe [discriminating behavior](discussion-and-design.md#record-requirements-at-the-useful-level), not just a feature name. Ordinary implementation details may be resolved within the selected method; a material open choice remains open unless the user decides or delegates it.

Maintained specifications describe intended behavior, while code and execution evidence establish actual behavior and current human instructions establish authority. Keep these sources connected without treating any one as a substitute for the others. Update the effective specification when a change is adopted, preserve the relevant prior basis, and identify unimplemented target behavior. Producing a proposal, design or task list does not itself adopt its choices or authorize implementation, model calls, data changes or publication.

## Choose a durable design

Before selecting an initial project design, designing a substantial capability before implementation, or materially changing the selected architecture, framework responsibilities or major interactions, research applicable official documentation and relevant established products or implementations. Compare how they solve the problem, their assumptions and limits, and adopt suitable proven patterns and conventions. Record the reasons for consequential departures. Research informs the choice; do not select a solution first and then seek only supporting examples. Reuse earlier research after checking version and problem applicability; routine edits need no new survey. Respect access limits and disclose missing sources and their effect on the decision.

Choose the simplest complete, maintainable implementation within agreed requirements, the selected architecture and known evolution needs. Compare functional effectiveness, reliability, output quality, autonomy where applicable, and development, integration and maintenance costs across the known delivery path. Do not save effort now by omitting known necessary boundaries or integration capabilities and leaving foreseeable replacement work to later increments. Avoid speculative abstractions, configuration and indirection for unselected possibilities. Neither the smallest patch, preserving current internals nor adopting a general framework is inherently preferable.

Identify relevant existing capabilities and dependencies before choosing reuse, extension, adoption or replacement. Check the installed or selected version's official documentation, types and relevant examples before concluding that a dependency lacks a capability. Use suitable existing dependencies before introducing equivalent custom code or another package. Prefer established, well-maintained libraries when they reduce overall complexity or improve reliability, accounting for integration, deployment and maintenance costs. Reimplement common functionality or add a package only with a concrete reason; checking capability does not authorize installation or upgrade.

Separate concerns and keep components modular around actual responsibilities, data/state ownership, changes and verification needs. More files, interfaces or layers do not by themselves establish better separation. Use [file ownership and placement](artifacts-and-storage.md#choose-ownership-before-creating-files) when creating assets, including framework-required locations, package-local owners and direct placement of adopted work; ordinary choices under an established map need no new design round.

When an important interface choice has materially different viable solutions, use [concrete interface comparison](discussion-and-design.md#compare-interface-alternatives). Favor useful behavior behind understandable interfaces and localize related changes; do not impose a universal module shape or speculative abstraction.

Implement the selected framework roles, design and project conventions rather than bypassing them for local convenience. For uncertain or version-sensitive API behavior, verify applicable official guidance. New requirements, code analysis or experiments can justify restructuring or revising the baseline before a production failure; distinguish supported limitations from expected benefits. A later requirement that warrants redesign does not alone invalidate the earlier choice. Assess affected contracts, integration, data and recovery, record material revisions and apply the human-decision boundary in [Fit the actual task](../SKILL.md#fit-the-actual-task) before dependent implementation. Ordinary details within the chosen method need no new approval.

Reassess flawed, incomplete or outdated requirements and compatibility assumptions. Establish what must be preserved, who depends on it and why. Backward compatibility is a project policy, not a universal obligation: where it is not required, remove obsolete paths instead of adding compatibility layers, fallbacks or unnecessary migrations. Propose changes to explicit requirements with their impacts and any necessary transition; implement only within applicable human authority. Preserve user data and useful results independently of old internal structure.

Do not deliver a knowingly temporary substitute that must be replaced to meet already-known requirements or the selected architecture. Prototypes, containment and transition work need an explicit purpose, applicable authorization and exit conditions; they do not establish completion of the durable implementation. Record their limits without using them as a general exception to quality or design commitments.

## Connect tasks, implementation and evidence

For each meaningful work item, identify the requirement, confirmed defect or necessary dependency it serves, the responsible component, relevant ordering and an observable finish. For each key preserved guarantee, state its applicable conditions, expected outcome, discriminating check and evidence status. In design or assessment, supply planned checks even when execution is outside authority. Reuse existing requirement/case identifiers and the project's task owner. Small repairs can use a few sentences; larger changes can use a table. Do not require a new tracking system, an identifier for every line or a task per internal edit.

Make the correspondence usable in both directions: important requirements lead to the implementation and checks, and planned or completed work leads back to its purpose. For verification, identify the actual result and code/specification basis, not only a test name or link. Distinguish planned, executed, partial, missing and inapplicable coverage using the project's terms. A task checkbox or a list of links alone does not show that the behavior is established. Store the correspondence under the [increment/task recording rules](records-and-handoff.md#record-the-increment-basis-and-task-owner), with detailed evidence in its existing owner.

When a guarantee spans entry points or transitions, identify which conclusions must agree and which differences the contract allows. For example, the same evidence under the same validation basis may need the same acceptance judgment on initial receipt and reopening. Checking that fields or rejection text survived does not establish that judgment. Different inputs, policy versions or authority can justify different outcomes; state those conditions rather than imposing universal equality. Preserve historical facts separately from a newly authorized reassessment.

Before handing off the scoped result, check whether the proposed or executed evidence could detect a violation of each key guarantee. Replace vague activities such as "test reopening" with an observable expected result or an explicit unresolved gap. Resolve omissions within the current authority; an unselected material policy remains a decision, not an invented expectation. This is a completion check in the same task, not an additional review, document or approval stage.

For example, a streaming receiver change might use:

| Requirement | Implementation responsibility | Discriminating evidence | Conclusion to establish |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Allow specified metadata updates while preserving response identity | Field classification and assembly in the decoder | Allowed-update examples; identity conflicts and missing required completion evidence | Which variations are accepted/rejected and under which limits; accepting metadata does not prove reply completeness |
| Use consistent rules on first acceptance and reopen | Acceptance and persisted-evidence validation paths | The same relevant evidence exercised through both paths | Consistent, inconsistent or not yet verified, tied to the actual versions and observations |
| Deliver the complete requested PDF conversion | Agent through saved, reopened and exported products | Actual complete artifacts checked against the source | Product completion or the remaining gap; parser checks cannot establish this outcome |

Look for a rule without implementation, implementation without adequate checks, evidence supporting only part of a condition, or work lacking a selected purpose or necessary dependency. Use these gaps to guide the scoped next action. Tasks implement the adopted requirements; adding tasks does not create new requirements.

## Verify the outcome

Derive checks from requirements and the affected responsibility, not only the reported failure or the implementation's chosen path. When shared behavior changes, check representative related operations and transitions. Select useful automated tests, focused manual checks, integration paths, or real-output inspection proportionately; a small copy edit may need only visual inspection. Do not add tests that merely repeat implementation details or require every possible combination.

Distinguish implementation, successful build, passing tests, actual user-flow verification, and release/deployment. Lead progress reports with what the user can now accomplish, which obstacle is resolved, what remains unverified and why the next action advances the goal. Test counts, document counts and completed repair batches are supporting evidence, not substitutes for outcomes. For design, maintenance or safety tasks, use their authorized decision or assurance outcome rather than requiring a visible UI feature. Report the state actually checked and preserve meaningful tests; correct a faulty expectation only with evidence for the intended behavior.

A specification and tests derived from it can share the same mistaken premise. Check relevant governing sources, counterexamples and actual product results; agreement between them is not independent proof. Keep a reproduced case, the affected capability and the phase/product outcome distinct. This developer workflow does not prescribe a runtime agent's tool sequence or reduce its agreed autonomy.

For failures, investigate the observation and competing causes before selecting or repeating changes. Use [problem framing and shared causes](debugging-and-learning.md#examine-problem-framing-and-shared-causes) to check relevant premises and the repair level, even on a first occurrence. Preserve usable work, failed observations, uncertainty and the necessary scene under [evidence retention](artifacts-and-storage.md#select-evidence-and-clean-up-within-authority). Choose the next action to resolve an actual unknown within the user's constraints.

For difficult diagnosis, questionable premises, recurring defects, cross-layer failures, interpreting metrics or reusing evidence, repeated experiments, or independent review, read the relevant sections of [Debugging and learning](debugging-and-learning.md). Routine fixes do not require that full reference.

## Resolve differences and converge

When specification, implementation or evidence disagree, identify the kind of difference before changing either the code or the requirement:

| Difference | Response |
| --- | --- |
| Implementation violates the adopted behavior | Fix the responsible mechanism within authority and verify the affected behavior and regression case. |
| Specification is wrong, ambiguous or rests on an unsupported assumption | Check governing requirements, sources and counterexamples. Explain the correction and impact; obtain the applicable decision for material changes unless delegated. Do not rewrite the spec merely to match current code, or reject supported corrections merely because the spec already exists. |
| Evidence is missing, insufficient or based on a faulty expectation | Select a discriminating check or substantiate the corrected expectation. If execution is not authorized, retain the unknown and continue independent permitted work; do not turn missing evidence into a pass. |
| A new requirement or improvement is proposed | Record the problem/value, evidence, tradeoffs and revisit condition. Include it only when selected and authorized, not because it was discovered during this batch. |

Before adding work from a completion check, distinguish a necessary gap in the adopted outcome, a supported blocker to correct or safe continuation, and a separate improvement. Repair necessary gaps together within the authorized batch. A serious supported risk may block continuation before harm occurs; it still does not authorize an out-of-scope remedy. Preserve all meaningful findings and decisions under [the existing record rules](records-and-handoff.md#track-discoveries-without-expanding-the-current-work), keeping evidence, severity, disposition and authority separate under [Review](review.md#reconcile-findings-with-evidence). Unrelated improvements remain available for separate selection.

Accept the increment when its adopted completion conditions have sufficient evidence and no supported blocker remains. Check preserved guarantees, relevant failure/recovery paths and unintended changes beyond scope. A known failure of required behavior remains an unmet condition, even if called an edge case. Identify residual unknowns, partial verification and deferred findings without requiring proof of zero possible defects. More tests or completed tasks cannot replace missing outcome evidence; repeat or broaden checks when changes, failures or unresolved concerns justify it.

Once the scoped obstacle is resolved, return to the product work it was blocking. Do not turn each new non-blocking observation into another prerequisite, review round or handoff. If evidence changes a material method, responsibility or requirement, return that choice to the appropriate decision point; ordinary repairs stay in the same authorized increment.

## Close or revise a phase

At each increment completion, assess the whole phase's accumulated changes against current effective requirements, intended outcome and adopted scope; do not assess only the latest addition. Compare the phase's starting scope and explicitly adopted revisions. Reconcile affected work-register entries, including partial completion and remaining validation, and consult consequential outstanding work before proposing continuation. Check whether added work is necessary, dependencies remain justified, completion conditions keep moving, and the next phase still makes sense. Finishing the latest increment does not automatically advance to the next activity in an old plan. Scale the depth to the change, risk and available evidence without skipping these questions. At a significant review, or when new evidence or material/cumulative scope growth warrants it, deepen the reassessment. Distinguish underestimated effort from added scope or a newly understood architectural cause. Choose what to retain, defer, move, split or replace, and record material changes within the task's write authority. A routine increment may need only a concise assessment, not a fresh full-phase audit. Current requirements may include human-approved changes; the initial document is not permanently binding.

Growth triggers reassessment, not automatic splitting at a fixed effort multiplier or conversation count. Split phases when this creates independently verifiable outcomes or milestones that resolve important uncertainty. If the parts must work together to satisfy the original delivery condition, preserve that integrated condition; new labels alone do not establish completion. Hypothetical risks need not all be eliminated before other useful work proceeds. Once effective completion conditions are evidenced and no supported blocking issue remains, close the phase within record-write authority. Preserve remaining non-blocking findings with their disposition and revisit conditions; their continued discovery does not indefinitely extend the phase.

Preserve agreed outcomes and quality constraints. Do not weaken completion conditions to label unfinished work complete, or erase failed checks and unresolved work when revising a phase. Distinguish a reproduced case being fixed, an affected capability being verified under its supported conditions, and the phase's outcome being achieved. Closing reported findings or increasing test counts does not establish all three. At phase closeout, check the whole delivered outcome against its completion conditions, not only its latest increment. Known failures of required behavior remain unmet conditions even if labeled edge cases; hypothetical unknowns alone do not require indefinite expansion. Completion means sufficient evidence for the scoped outcome, not a promise of zero future defects or a final repair. Keep functional verification, integration, synchronization and publication distinct. If integration or publication is part of this phase's agreed outcome, it belongs in acceptance; otherwise it is not an added completion gate.

At verified phase completion, proactively check recoverable checkpoints and pending synchronization/integration, and assess a useful tag or release under [Git workflow](git-workflow.md). Perform appropriate already-authorized actions or give a concrete reminder. Retain completion anchors and pending work under [phase records](records-and-handoff.md#maintain-a-rolling-phase-plan). Completion triggers this assessment, not a mandatory tag/release or new publication authority; the absence of a tag or release is not itself unfinished work.

When later evidence or recovery affects a completion claim, preserve original measurements and the artifacts needed to interpret them under [evidence retention](artifacts-and-storage.md#select-evidence-and-clean-up-within-authority), link the new finding, and correct the affected current claim within the task's write authority. Authorized reduction must disclose changed evidence availability, not rewrite the earlier result. Distinguish:

- A regression introduced in a later revision: retain earlier valid verification and track the later regression and remedy.
- Evidence that the earlier acceptance was insufficient or mistaken: qualify or correct the earlier completion claim, retaining what was actually tested. Reopen affected work or arrange a follow-up according to the completion conditions; do not keep an unmet outcome marked complete merely to avoid reopening it.
- Rolling the current version back: update current capabilities, version and rollback reason. This alone does not invalidate another version's historical verification.

Do not silently move a tag to rewrite the version associated with old evidence. Update the relevant claim or version note, and connect selected follow-up work to the active plan; no automatic new phase or fixed status label is required.

## Maintain documents throughout the work

Automatically maintain the necessary documents for the selected project or skill task, including ordinary orientation, discussion, spec preparation, ticket planning, standalone review and implementation. The user need not request `document` at every transition. "Discuss first" limits the activity to discussion and its necessary documents. Interpret an explicit response-only, read-only, no-file-changes instruction or higher-priority mode restriction as a write limit and provide pending content instead. General questions and prompt drafting use their response scope unless project maintenance is requested or already part of the work.

Use the existing topic and work owners. Save at meaningful changes, with enough context for another contributor to understand the outcome and its reasons.

| Trigger | What to preserve and when |
| --- | --- |
| Substantive discussion develops | After a meaningful exchange or group of related exchanges, update the problem, constraints, attributed options, reasons, disagreements and open questions. Keep the current view and consequential changes retrievable. |
| A decision is made or revised | Before dependent work, save the selected rule, rationale, implications, adoption basis and any superseded choice. Reconcile the affected effective design once adopted. |
| A supported finding or important limitation is identified | Save the evidence, impact, uncertainty and disposition when assessed, even while the remedy remains open. Link consequential outstanding work in the register. |
| A spec or task plan becomes ready | Save the agreed outcome, preserved guarantees, acceptance and applicable execution boundary. Connect tickets, dependencies and responsibilities to their spec. Keep unresolved parts visibly draft or blocked. |
| Implementation or review changes readiness | At a meaningful increment or integration boundary, update task progress, actual checks and results, corrections, residual gaps and affected design explanations. |
| Focus, next activity or its authority changes | Save the substantive outcome, then update [CURRENT_STATE](#maintain-current-focus-and-resume-context). Preserve the interrupted work's resume point before switching; do not wait for an explicit handoff. |
| Delivery or handoff approaches | Reconcile changed owners, affected acceptance/selection decisions and usable routes so continuation can recover scope, progress, evidence and remaining work without copied summaries. |

Batch routine progress updates at these boundaries. The user may leave without warning: save meaningful discussion and confirmed findings when they form, and important decisions before dependent execution. Reuse accurate records, merge repetition and omit transient thoughts and ordinary coding minutiae. A meaningful correction, rejected alternative or reason for changing direction remains useful context. Report actual updated locations at a useful checkpoint or closeout. Git checkpoints follow [Git workflow](git-workflow.md#authority-and-project-policy) and the current task's authority.

Update substantive owners first, then affected tasks/decisions, then navigation and CURRENT_STATE where their own facts change. Inspect dependent claims under [one-owner maintenance](documentation-structure.md#keep-one-owner-per-fact); a valid link does not keep its surrounding explanation accurate automatically. Leave unaffected content untouched. If a write fails or only some destinations are updated, retain the exact pending change and known state in a permitted existing owner or the response; do not claim synchronization or point to nonexistent saved content. The main agent coordinates one writer/integrator for shared owners under authorized delegation.

For a GitHub-backed batch, use these boundaries within the current destination authority:

| Transition | Owner update and linked continuation |
| --- | --- |
| Discussion becomes an adopted rule | Preserve the decision and its rationale; update the governing spec before dependent work. Parent/tickets link that rule. A stable link needs no edit merely because the rule's content changed. |
| Spec becomes ready for work splitting | Save scope and criteria in the batch's `spec.md`. Maintain the separate `tickets.md` according to the project ticket mode; parent/execution Issues link the spec and own their dependencies, responsibility and progress. |
| Implementation or review changes execution | Implementers update their assigned code/tests and technical owners in their task branches. Main agent integrates the changed documents with the code and updates the issue that owns execution state. Shared WORK_ITEMS/CURRENT_STATE changes have one integrator. |
| Evidence changes or acceptance is assessed | Save new batch observations and the combined verdict in `verification.md`, linking existing evidence owners rather than copying their results. Issues/PRs link it. Close eligible issues within authority; reassess only distinct project-wide readiness or selection decisions that the new evidence affects. |
| Handoff, interruption or next-session resume | Check relevant owner content, source versions and link accessibility. Preserve only necessary unresolved destination updates in the existing work owner; reread current remote state before applying them. Resolve conflicts by authority, meaning and evidence, not the newest timestamp. |

Repository docs are edited locally and versioned with the applicable code under [Git workflow](git-workflow.md); issue changes are separate remote operations. Main-agent coordination does not install a background sync service or make the two updates atomic. If a permitted remote update cannot be confirmed, record its intended destination/change and actual known state in the existing owner: distinguish an unsent operation from an attempted operation with an unknown outcome. Do not create a second live issue ledger. Continue independent authorized work, verify the destination before retrying, then resolve the pending entry once confirmed. Explicit no-write limits use [pending records](#when-record-writes-are-unavailable). Do not claim that an unpublished branch document is already accessible from GitHub.

For a batch using the fixed layout, keep a bounded pending GitHub operation in a clearly labeled temporary section of `tickets.md`: destination, unsent or unconfirmed operation, intended change and known remote basis. This exception to link-only navigation is an operation draft, not a local execution ledger or ticket-mode switch. New Issue payloads can remain explicitly unpublished here until creation is authorized and confirmed; replace resolved drafts with ID/Issue links. Other records link the operation without copying its pending state. For a legacy batch outside migration scope, use its identified existing coordination owner. When no permitted file destination exists, provide pending content in the response.

Automatic documentation covers the task's discussion, decisions, findings and progress. Recording an option preserves its proposal status. Update effective requirements only after the choice is adopted, and keep adopted, implemented and verified states distinct. Local maintenance grants no new authority for code execution, external publication or changes to user data. For connected documents, follow the destination's access and write rules and the user's selected scope.

## Keep documents current during daily work

Apply this within ordinary implementation, review and actual handoff; the user need not invoke `document`. The main agent owns the necessary maintenance through the same scoped work, including related claims in files that are absent from the diff. Use [one-owner links](documentation-structure.md#keep-one-owner-per-fact) and the [fixed batch files](batch-documents.md). This is part of delivery, not an additional user approval stage or a new documentation ledger.

Read the rule for a coordination owner before changing it, reusing applicable guidance already read: [CURRENT_STATE](#maintain-current-focus-and-resume-context) for interaction changes; [WORK_ITEMS](#maintain-the-project-work-register) for selection/disposition; [PHASE_PLAN](#maintain-a-rolling-phase-plan) for phase changes; [INDEX](documentation-structure.md#make-records-discoverable) for navigation. Do not read all four merely because one changes. A new batch result alone does not require updating all four.

**At entry or resume, establish the basis.** Follow [task-based reading](documentation-structure.md#read-by-task-and-follow-dependencies), then reconcile inherited edits and applicable decisions with actual source/evidence state. Identify likely documentation consumers from the selected behavior before implementation, so checks cover more than files already edited. Classify a mismatch: an adopted target awaiting implementation, an implementation defect, an obsolete current description, or an evidence gap. Code is evidence of actual behavior, not authority to weaken a requirement; a document's age alone does not make it obsolete.

**As meaningful changes occur, follow the changed meaning.** Identify the behavior, interface, configuration, selection, execution state or evidence that changed. Search its concepts/synonyms, names, work IDs, source paths and incoming references across relevant active documentation, including unchanged README/setup guides, technical guides and continuation records. Use topic navigation as well: a consumer may have no link or exact matching phrase. Inspect default values, commands, examples, failure instructions, terminology and acceptance statements whose meaning depends on the change. Update the substantive owner and affected distinct claims/decisions; replace redundant active definitions with links. The diff and inbound links are discovery aids, not the maintenance boundary. Save consequential decisions before dependent work; batch routine progress at useful boundaries.

**Before delivery or handoff, check meaning and navigation.** Trace an affected claim to its rule and applicable source/evidence version, then use existing path/anchor checks and a focused [reader/change check](documentation-structure.md#verify-document-usability). Simulate one fact changing without editing real records: which other current sentences would need rewriting solely to restate a ticket's progress or verification verdict? Replace those copies with links, including new prose produced in this task. Calling a batch pass "accepted work disposition" in WORK_ITEMS or "readiness" elsewhere still duplicates the verdict; a distinct planning decision must add scope, priority, dependencies or reconsideration information. Check the corrected documents, not only wording removed. Valid links and passing code tests do not establish current prose. During authorized delivery, correct supported in-scope stale claims before claiming completion.

Preserve historical observations with their original code/spec/input basis; add a linked correction or supersession explanation when necessary rather than rewriting an old run as a new pass. An old passing run does not validate changed behavior. Keep adopted-but-unimplemented targets explicit, and label unsupported current claims unverified until their evidence is established. Retire obsolete active guidance through a clear replacement route while preserving consequential reasons and historical evidence. Do not delete all old prose or merge distinct facts merely because they share words.

Keep the work proportional to the changed surface. A behavior, default, interface or acceptance change warrants checking its consumers; a bounded internal change may leave descriptions valid. Do not manufacture edits, refresh timestamps as proof, require a full-project audit per ticket, or create another batch/file per check. In the existing batch `verification.md`, or applicable review owner, record a concise **Documentation impact**: changed facts, affected owners/consumers inspected, corrections or reasons no change was needed, and unresolved limits. Link the actual sections and evidence; a declaration that "docs are current" or a list of read filenames does not establish semantic coverage.

Scope still governs actions. Standalone review assesses affected claims and maintains permitted findings/records; it does not silently become implementation or general cleanup. Read-only review and response-only prompt drafting produce findings or pending corrections without file edits. Actual handoff can reconcile its necessary current records but cannot run the next task by implication. Unrelated stale material receives a bounded finding and disposition; it does not expand the current batch. Material requirement choices stay with their applicable decision process while independent authorized work continues.

## Maintain current focus and resume context

Use CURRENT_STATE as a short, replaceable continuation record, not a chat transcript, backlog, spec or result summary. The focus may be an unresolved question, direction discussion, spec preparation, implementation, diagnosis or review. Do not force unfinished discussion into a batch merely to make it trackable. Preserve substantive content in its topic or batch owner, then keep these facts findable when they matter:

```markdown
# Current state

Current focus: <topic or selected work identifier>
Resume at: <existing owner and exact section>
Next activity: <agreed activity, or explicitly unselected recommendation>
Instruction basis: <attributed user instruction and applicable limits>
Return to: <parked work's owner/section, when relevant>
```

This illustrates responsibilities, not mandatory keys or a new state machine. Link the detailed decision/authority basis where it is already maintained rather than copying it. Keep only enough instruction context to distinguish what can resume; do not convert an assistant recommendation, spec readiness or old permission into current authority. Avoid copied ticket progress, test counts, verdicts and full design summaries. PHASE_PLAN owns phase acceptance, WORK_ITEMS owns project selection/disposition, and the batch owners retain execution and evidence.

| Interaction event | Durable content and continuation |
| --- | --- |
| Discussion remains unresolved | Save meaningful options, constraints and the exact open question in the discussion owner. Resume there, with discussion as the activity. |
| Direction is selected but details remain open | Record adoption/reasons and unresolved specification choices; CURRENT_STATE points to specification work only when that activity is selected. Agreement with direction alone does not authorize implementation. |
| `spec.md` is complete | Save the agreement and planned acceptance. Resume at task planning or implementation only under the applicable instruction; if the user said to wait, record that boundary. Do not create empty tickets or fabricated verification. |
| Implementation starts or encounters a bug | Tickets own execution; verification owns observed failure and its version; material open behavior belongs in discussion/design. If the user changes the activity to discussion, point there and preserve the implementation resume point. Ordinary scoped defects remain in authorized delivery without another permission ceremony. |
| Work is parked or switched | Save its last useful state, exact open question/next step and necessary source/artifact identities in the existing work owner. Change CURRENT_STATE's focus and retain a return link. Parking does not by itself defer, reject, cancel or reprioritize WORK_ITEMS. |
| Work finishes or the user stops | Link the acceptance owner and keep any remaining continuation explicit. If no next activity is selected, say so and route selection to WORK_ITEMS/PHASE_PLAN; do not silently start a recommendation. |
| A new chat resumes | Reconcile the current request with CURRENT_STATE and its linked owners. Inspect actual code/evidence before relying on readiness. A named task overrides a different saved focus; vague continuation follows the recorded activity if unambiguous. |

Update CURRENT_STATE when its focus, resume destination, next activity or instruction basis changes, not after every command. Keep parked work details in their own owners, with only useful return routes here; do not append an ever-growing session log. Ordinary Git history is enough for routine pointer changes. If concurrent chats have distinct active work, identify the relevant workstream/checkout and coordinate a shared writer rather than letting last-write time select a winner. Ask only when the intended continuation remains consequentially ambiguous.

## Record an outcome in its owners

An explicit `document` or "update the relevant docs" request selects focused synchronization for the current subject, including important content left only in conversation. Necessary updates also happen under [automatic documentation](#maintain-documents-throughout-the-work) and [handoff closeout](#draft-prompts-and-handoffs-without-expanding-authority). Locate the actual owners and preserve meaningful findings, decisions, evidence, reasons, corrections, open choices and disposition. Update changed owners and dependent decisions, replacing redundant active summaries with links within scope; do not merely prepend the whole conversation. Existing accurate entries and valid links need no rewrite, and ordinary recording needs no new document hierarchy.

Use [decision recording](#record-decisions-before-dependent-work), [discoveries](#track-discoveries-without-expanding-the-current-work) and [version preservation](documentation-structure.md#preserve-versions-at-defined-events) as applicable. A decision may be adopted while implementation or verification remains pending. Record unadopted options as such; do not use record maintenance to settle a material choice, implement code, rewrite raw evidence or change execution authority. Useful lessons belong with their supporting project evidence; updating a general skill is separate work unless requested.

Complete the permitted updates and report document names, full paths/resource links and relevant sections/IDs. For handoff, use the resulting records in the continuation prompt without another approval round. Apply the pending-record rule below wherever necessary updates remain unwritten, including implementation closeout and review.

### When record writes are unavailable

For a necessary update that cannot be saved under current authority, provide the entry itself in the response, ready to incorporate into its owner. Identify the document's full path or exact resource link and relevant section/ID, and label the text **pending, not saved**. If the owner is unconfirmed, distinguish a proposed destination from an inspected existing owner; do not invent a file, fact or decision to make the entry look complete.

Include the minimum context needed to understand and maintain that outcome: the consequential prior observation and reason or impact, what changed or was decided, actual checks/results and their limits, and any unresolved evidence or local-only dependency. Include only what applies to the affected record. Reuse adequate maintained explanations by link; when the necessary explanation exists only in ignored files, a package or chat, carry the relevant permitted facts into the pending text rather than only pointing to that local source. Preserve unknowns, historical scope, private-data limits and proposed/adopted/implemented/verified distinctions.

A task such as "update verification later" is not pending record content. A self-contained review finding or result paragraph can itself be the entry when its owner and unsaved status are clear; do not repeat it in a second draft. Small changes may need only a few sentences. Do not draft whole documents, add a hierarchy or manufacture an update when existing records already suffice.

Continue independent authorized work and any permitted handoff. Do not write a sidecar file to evade a write restriction, claim the content is saved or synchronized, or repeatedly request permission for expressly excluded effects. When recording is later authorized, reconcile the pending text with current owners and evidence before applying it; preparing the text does not authorize that later write.

## Record decisions before dependent work

At a consequential transition, identify what changed in the decision or evidence and whether existing records preserve enough context for the next task. Apply the transition rule in [Fit the actual task](../SKILL.md#fit-the-actual-task); recording is part of preparing that work, not only its closeout.

Before implementing behavior that depends on a material rule, clarify the rule, relevant responsibilities and how correctness will be checked. Resolve consequential ambiguity through applicable evidence or a decision under [Fit the actual task](../SKILL.md#fit-the-actual-task); do not let code silently settle open policy, permission, data-handling or major design choices. Ordinary implementation details and unknowns that do not invalidate the current work can be resolved within the authorized increment. This does not require completing all project documents before coding or approving each detail. Continue independent authorized work while a material choice is pending.

Within record-write authority, capture the selected direction and rationale, supporting evidence and limits, unresolved options, and the next action's scope, authority and completion condition in the existing owner before dependent execution. Keep adopted direction, authorized execution and verified results distinct. Update only affected owners; a short entry and link may suffice, and already-current records need no rewrite. Read-only inspection needed to make the entry accurate can precede it. If an experiment is needed to resolve the rule, establish its question, scope, authority and stopping conditions under [Make an experiment informative](debugging-and-learning.md#make-an-experiment-informative); its result does not automatically become an adopted contract. No new document set, commit or approval ceremony is required.

Interpret short replies against the actual proposal and current mode. For example:

| Situation | Appropriate continuation |
| --- | --- |
| The user agrees with a diagnostic direction and asks what comes next during ordinary project discussion. | Record the selected direction and remaining uncertainty, then explain or undertake only the next work actually authorized. Save the decision before dependent work. |
| The same exchange occurs under a no-file-changes instruction or a side-chat write restriction. | Supply [pending record content](#when-record-writes-are-unavailable) and include recording in the proposed handoff. Skill invocation does not override that restriction or authorize messaging another conversation. |
| The exchange is a small clarification, or the relevant decision and authority are already accurately recorded. | Answer or continue within scope without a redundant entry or another confirmation. |

Use the [pending-record rule](#when-record-writes-are-unavailable) for a necessary unwritten decision; do not silently defer the gap past a handoff.

## Record the increment basis and task owner

Use the [fixed batch directory and project ticket mode](batch-documents.md). The separate `spec.md` owns the agreement, `tickets.md` owns local execution details or Issue navigation, and `verification.md` owns observed evidence or evidence links plus the combined verdict. Report actual paths and sections, distinguishing planned files from those created. Link the batch from selected work items and active-work navigation. PHASE_PLAN owns product direction and phase acceptance, WORK_ITEMS owns distinct item dispositions, and CURRENT_STATE owns interaction continuity. Topic designs retain adopted technical rules. Keep the full batch plan out of WORK_ITEMS and link substantive owners instead of copying their content.

For [GitHub-backed execution](github-issues.md#choose-the-ownership-map), Issues own task details and coordination; the batch's `tickets.md` is their stable ID/link entrance. Link `spec.md` and `verification.md` without repeating their contents. Update a local register/readiness decision only when its own fact changes; native issue progress remains on GitHub. Select the task system once for the project, not per batch. Changing it requires a deliberate migration and does not silently migrate the project work register or grant remote write authority.

A small repair uses the same three separate destinations with concise content, created when their stages have substance. A cross-topic batch links its normative topic rules from `spec.md`; it does not copy those rules or mix the actual verdict into planned criteria. Drafts remain visibly unresolved; adopted but unimplemented behavior remains visibly unfinished. Track ready/active/blocked work, implementation awaiting integration and accepted work in the execution owner, with the relevant basis and evidence rather than mandatory labels.

Record what the work needs to distinguish:

| Information | What must remain findable |
| --- | --- |
| Reference baseline | Applicable requirement/design/shared-contract revisions and the actual source/work state used for comparison |
| Adopted change | Selected target behavior, preserved guarantees, scope and completion conditions, with the decision and authority that apply |
| Actual readiness | Implemented, verified, partial or unresolved behavior, tied to observed code state and evidence rather than inferred from adoption |
| Execution plan | Meaningful tasks and necessary dependencies, responsibilities, integration order and observable finish, at the useful level of detail |
| Coverage | Important requirement -> implementation -> check/result relationships, gaps and limits; work can also be traced back to its requirement, defect or necessary dependency |

Use [Specification basis](implementation.md#establish-the-specification-basis) and [correspondence](implementation.md#connect-tasks-implementation-and-evidence) for the method. Keep detailed results with their verification owner and link exact runs, revisions and conditions rather than copying an evidence ledger. Planned checks are not results; earlier evidence does not automatically validate a changed version.

The topic design owns the adopted capability and its basis; the batch files describe work toward that target. Adding a task or running a check does not itself change design, requirements or authorization. Material design changes follow [version preservation](documentation-structure.md#preserve-versions-at-defined-events), [basis links](documentation-structure.md#bind-design-versions-to-their-basis) and reconciliation of affected current statements. Small repairs use concise prose and existing links within the fixed files; no additional document per task, approval round or per-turn rewrite is required. Use [pending records](#when-record-writes-are-unavailable) for necessary unsaved updates.

## Maintain a rolling phase plan

Use `docs/PHASE_PLAN.md` as the single project roadmap, established with the [core development records](documentation-structure.md#establish-the-development-entry) from project creation. It describes phase outcomes, sequencing and acceptance, while WORK_ITEMS identifies concrete outstanding work and CURRENT_STATE identifies the interaction's focus and resume point. A new small project can begin with one useful phase and brief later direction; it does not need a speculative multi-stage plan. Honor an explicitly selected equivalent without creating a second roadmap. A bounded repair in an existing project uses its actual owners and does not trigger an unrelated reorganization. Each project's live plan belongs in that project, not in this skill.

Use [project direction](implementation.md#keep-the-project-direction), [increment selection](implementation.md#choose-a-coherent-increment) and [phase completion](implementation.md#close-or-revise-a-phase) to select, assess and close work. This section owns the durable plan records; fine-grained tasks and coverage use the declared increment owner above.

Use concise prose or the project's existing format to record:

- **Outcome:** what becomes possible, linked to the relevant product requirements.
- **Selection rationale:** the problem or opportunity, supporting evidence or assumption, and why this stage has its proposed priority.
- **Scope and dependencies:** included work, deliberate exclusions and actual prerequisites.
- **Work connections:** relevant work-register IDs and their contribution to the phase. Item priority, selection/deferral reasons and revisit conditions stay in WORK_ITEMS; do not duplicate its backlog.
- **Completion conditions:** observable behavior and proportionate verification, linking to detailed acceptance criteria where they already have an owner.
- **Phase status:** assess the phase outcome against its conditions and actual evidence. Individual ticket or batch completion does not establish phase acceptance.
- **Material revisions:** briefly explain the previous intended outcome, new finding and evidence strength, resulting change, preserved requirements and how to check the revised approach. Link consequential rationale to its decision owner; routine edits need no separate decision record.

Preserve a retrievable baseline of each phase's starting outcome, scope and completion conditions, together with explicitly adopted revisions and their reasons. Existing version history or linked decisions can provide this; do not freeze the whole plan or require another baseline file.

The plan owns delivery structure, phase status and stable completion anchors linking scope, implementation identity, evidence and consequential decisions. Preserve these links when current work advances. WORK_ITEMS owns item dispositions and candidate next actions; CURRENT_STATE owns the current interaction's selected activity and resume route. Validation records own observations, revisions, conditions, results and limits. Git and release records identify saved or published versions and artifacts. Use [one-owner links](documentation-structure.md#keep-one-owner-per-fact). Reassess a phase when its outcome, scope, dependencies or acceptance basis changes; routine focus switches and ticket updates do not require plan edits or rerunning whole-phase acceptance.

At increment completion, reconcile changed items and readiness before applying [phase reassessment](implementation.md#close-or-revise-a-phase) and [next-work selection](implementation.md#choose-a-coherent-increment). Explain material changes to the plan or priority. A phase's name states an outcome, not the next operation to perform; a real-world validation phase may still need a corrective implementation increment first. Preserve justified deferrals without turning all open items into phase prerequisites.

At phase completion, retain the anchors in the concise phase entry and link detailed evidence to its owner. Within document-write authority, preserve pending synchronization or integration work in the current-state or work owner, rather than only in the chat closeout. Record affected work, the known destination or unresolved choice, observed status and next action; qualify synchronization observations by what was checked and when. Keep volatile counts in the immediate report unless needed for continuation, and recheck them when relevant. Report uncommitted, unsynchronized, untagged, unpublished or deferred status accurately when relevant. Use [Git's checkpoint guidance](git-workflow.md#preserve-work-and-make-useful-checkpoints) for version identities, without chasing the document's own latest commit SHA.

For later evidence, regressions or rollback affecting completion, apply [the completion-claim rules](implementation.md#close-or-revise-a-phase): preserve original observations and their version basis, correct affected current claims, and link selected follow-up work. Do not silently move a tag or create a new phase merely to express a status correction.

A plan entry does not authorize execution, model calls or external changes. Existing human authorization may cover several phases; follow it without inventing a new approval or independent-review gate at each boundary. Changes to explicit outcomes or constraints need the applicable human decision. During discussion or standalone review, save proposed plan changes with their proposal status under [automatic documentation](#maintain-documents-throughout-the-work). Apply adopted changes to the effective plan and use pending content when writes are restricted.

## Draft prompts and handoffs without expanding authority

An explicit `handoff`, or an unambiguous request to close the current work for another session, includes synchronizing its necessary documentation before producing the continuation prompt. Apply the [daily document check](#keep-documents-current-during-daily-work), then [outcome recording](#record-an-outcome-in-its-owners) for actual state, findings, adopted decisions, verification results and limits, and selected next work in their owners. Reconcile affected current statements and navigation; reuse accurate records. This is bounded record maintenance for the current subject, not a general document reorganization, a change of requirements, adoption of an open proposal or permission to implement the next task.

Explicit response-only, no-file-changes, read-only or other narrower instructions override that synchronization. Supply [pending content and exact owners](#when-record-writes-are-unavailable) for necessary unwritten records and continue the permitted handoff. An ordinary request to draft or revise a prompt remains a response task unless the user also requests project closeout or file updates; a project mention or the word "complete" alone does not authorize record writes. Neither form of prompt preparation creates/starts a chat, commits, publishes or executes the prompt unless requested under applicable authority.

Separate this closeout's authority from the next session's authority. In the continuation prompt, preserve the selected next task, its effective permissions and explicit restrictions, including whether necessary document maintenance is allowed and for what purpose. Interpret restrictions by their stated task or phase: a completed review's no-implementation limit does not negate later authorized implementation, while ongoing or explicit next-session limits still apply. Identify known document/section owners, or direct the receiving agent to locate them through project navigation; the user need not enumerate or reapprove each file. Current permission to synchronize handoff records does not itself grant document writes in a read-only next session. Conversely, carry forward already-authorized next-session record maintenance without requiring another approval. Distinguish document edits from application changes, task databases, originals, execution state, model calls and publication; permission for one does not establish permission for the others.

After a standalone review leaves the next activity unselected, use its [next-step guidance](review.md#improvement-batches-and-closeout) and the user's subsequent selection to prepare the appropriate continuation. Within an authorized delivery batch, carry the selected spec, unfinished tickets, scoped review corrections and integrated acceptance into any necessary handoff. When implementation is selected and authorized, the prompt should complete the bounded work, necessary verification and records; baseline reconciliation is preparation, not a proposal-only stopping point. Do not restart settled discussion or add a review stage for ordinary implementation details. If a material choice or decision-changing evidence is still missing, make that gap and the recommended discussion/check visible in the current exchange. Do not silently replace a requested implementation handoff with a proposal-only assignment, or present an unselected method as adopted; resolve the needed choice or hand off the narrower activity when the user selects it. This does not require discussion before every handoff or another approval for already-authorized work.

Preserve the agreed scope, constraints and actual authorization when drafting work instructions. A proposed next step, recorded finding or historical permission is not an execution instruction. If recommending an unselected mode or authority change, explain it outside the ready-to-use prompt for the user's decision; do not put it inside as granted permission.
